title: 3M and AWS collaborate to advance optical connectivity innovation
content_text:
3M and AWS collaborate to advance optical connectivity innovation
Oct 21, 2026 • 10:28 AM EDT 
Download as PDF
AWS is investing in 3M's Expanded Beam Optical technology for its data center infrastructure 
SAINT PAUL, Minn. , Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- 3M  (NYSE: MMM) and  Amazon Web Services (AWS) today announced an expanded strategic collaboration. AWS plans to deploy and scale 3M's Expanded Beam Optical (EBO) platform for its data center infrastructure. Together, the two leading American companies will advance co-innovation and investment in optical connectivity and the critical infrastructure needed for next-generation super intelligence (SI), also known as artificial intelligence (AI). 
"AWS's adoption of 3M's EBO platform demonstrates the potential of our optical connectivity technology to meet the performance demands of next-generation data center infrastructure," said Wendy Bauer, Group President of 3M's Transportation and Electronics Business Group. "By combining AWS's infrastructure expertise and scale with 3M's innovation and materials science capabilities, we can accelerate EBO deployment, advance our transformation and strengthen U.S. innovation and investment." 
"Our work with 3M reinforces our commitment to supporting good jobs here in the U.S.," said Jens Gruenkemeir, Vice President of Supply Chain & Procurement at Amazon. "Beyond powering the services people use every day, from online banking and hospital data records to streaming entertainment and retail purchases, our data center investments are unlocking economic opportunities in the communities where we invest and across the supply chain, including the hundreds of jobs being supported by 3M as a result of its collaboration with Amazon."   
The collaboration and related investments are expected to strengthen the U.S. economy by supporting more than 500 jobs directly and indirectly, including the creation of more than 100 new roles through 2027 across Minnesota, Texas and Wisconsin. These planned roles will support customer co-innovation, technology advancement and supply chain development across 3M's optical networking portfolio and help accelerate industrywide adoption through collaboration with partners. 
3M expects to contribute nearly $0.5 billion to the U.S. economy through its optical connectivity business. This investment will accelerate innovation in optical networking and fiber termination, enable commercialization at scale and drive adoption across the data center industry.
The collaboration builds on 3M's announcement earlier this year that it will double production capacity at its Menomonie, Wisconsin, manufacturing facility, and is expected to support U.S. manufacturing partners involved in equipment and production scale-up throughout the supply chain.

title: Infineon announces winners of the startup challenge on humanoid robotics
content_text:
Infineon announces winners of the startup challenge on humanoid robotics
Business & Financial Press
Oct 19, 2026 
AdapTronics S.r.l. from Italy wins Infineon's international startup challenge on humanoid robotics with an innovative gripping technology; COSMOKE from South Korea takes second place with its magnetic tactile sensing technology for physical AI, followed by TECHiFAB from Germany in third place with its intelligent motor control solution 
Over 100 startups from 29 countries participated in the challenge, 15 were selected to pitch their solutions enabling the next generation of humanoid robots and physical AI applications to an international jury 
The program provided access to Infineon technologies, expert mentoring, business coaching, and an international innovation network 
Munich, Germany – 19 October 2026 – Infineon has announced the winners of the Infineon Startup Challenge 2026, focused on key technologies for the next generation of humanoid robots. Following four months of intensive collaboration, development and mentoring, 15 selected startups out of more than 100 applicants presented their solutions at the Infineon Startup Challenge Demo Day, held during the Electronic Based Systems Conference (EBSCON) in Graz, Austria.
The challenge brought together startups from Europe and Asia, investors, industry experts and technology leaders to advance innovation in robotics and physical AI. Participants developed solutions that enable humanoid robots to better perceive and interact with their environment, manipulate objects, and perform precise movements. The winners were selected by an international jury comprising experts from industry, venture capital, startup ecosystems, and technology innovation.
“Strategic collaboration with startups creates a win-win situation, combining novel ideas with industrially proven semiconductor technologies and thereby accelerating innovative, market-ready applications,” said Sören Jehmlich, Vice President Ventures, Startups & Ecosystems at Infineon. “The Startup Challenge is a key pillar of our innovation culture, bringing together entrepreneurial courage, technological expertise and rapid implementation.”
"The quality of innovation we have seen throughout this year's challenge has been remarkable. Startups from Europe and Asia demonstrated how diverse perspectives and technologies can come together to solve some of the most important challenges in humanoid robotics. Programs like the Infineon Startup Challenge are essential for connecting innovators across regions and accelerating the path from breakthrough ideas to real-world impact," highlights Jerry Park, Director Asia Pacific at Infineon .
The winners are shaping the future of humanoid robotics 
First place went to AdapTronics S.r.l. from Italy with its innovative gripping technology, which allows robots to safely handle a wide variety of objects without conventional suction cups or mechanical grippers. Such flexible object handling is a key capability for next-generation humanoid robots. The technology also addresses applications in logistics, packaging, and future space-robotics. The jury highlighted its versatility, innovation, and potential for industrial use. “Winning the Infineon Startup Challenge is a great recognition of our team’s work and vision,” said Lorenzo Agostini, Founder and CEO at AdapTronics S.r.l. “The challenge gave us valuable access to technology experts, industry insights and a strong innovation network. We look forward to further advancing our solution and exploring new opportunities for collaboration.”
COSMOKE and TECHiFAB complete the podium 
Second place went to COSMOKE from South Korea . The startup developed COSKIN, an innovative flexible magnetic tactile sensing technology that enables humanoid robots to perceive touch, pressure, and physical interactions. By providing essential tactile feedback for dexterous manipulation and safer human robot interaction, COSKIN plays a key role in advancing next-generation humanoid robotics and physical AI.
TECHiFAB from Germany took third place with its In-Memory Computing based approach to real-time motor control for robotic actuators. This is physical AI by definition and is designed to enable faster, more energy-efficient and safer control while improving performance directly within the drive train of humanoid robots.
The solutions presented during the challenge reflect the technologies required for the next generation of humanoid robots, from tactile sensing to dexterous gripping and precise motor control. To support the startups in developing and validating their concepts, Infineon provided access to dedicated hardware and software platforms, including Environmental Sensing Kits, Artificial Skin Kits, Motor Control Kits, Visual Feedback Kits, and in-house AI development software, enabling teams to accelerate prototyping and transform innovative ideas into scalable applications.
“Humanoid robots are the most complex form of physical AI and highly relevant for Infineon," said Dirk Geiger, Senior Director & Team Lead Humanoid Robotics at Infineon. “They combine power, sensing, real-time connectivity, safety and security with software and AI compute, turning machines into autonomous systems. No single company can master this complexity alone. With the Startup Challenge, we gave startups early access to our hardware stack as well as our software and system offering and brought them together with our partners and application experts. The solutions shown prove how quickly ideas can become building blocks for scalable humanoid platforms and give valuable insight into where the technology is heading."
The Infineon Startup Challenge is part of the global Infineon Startup Co-Innovation Program, in which Infineon collaborates with startups as a technology and development partner. As the winner of the Infineon Startup Challenge 2026, AdapTronics will now join the Infineon Startup Co-Innovation Program to further develop and scale its solution together with Infineon. The collaboration will officially kick off at the Startup Night in Munich in November, where Infineon showcases successful startup partnerships and highlights the value of startup-driven innovation. Infineon continues to engage with other promising participants for future technological and business collaboration. By combining the agility and creativity of startups with Infineon’s technological expertise and global capabilities, the program supports the development of scalable applications and accelerates innovation in humanoid robotics and physical AI. 
About Infineon
Infineon Technologies AG is a global semiconductor leader in power systems and IoT. Infineon drives decarbonization and digitalization with its products and solutions. The Company had around 57,000 employees worldwide (end of September 2025) and generated revenue of about €14.7 billion in the 2025 fiscal year (ending 30 September). Infineon is listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange (ticker symbol: IFX) and in the USA on the OTCQX International over-the-counter market (ticker symbol: IFNNY).

title: BASF signs Letter of Intent with Taiwan’s Ministry of Economic Affairs to advance next-generation semiconductor manufacturing
content_text:
BASF signs Letter of Intent with Taiwan’s Ministry of Economic Affairs to advance next-generation semiconductor manufacturing
Establishing new production capacity for semiconductor materials supporting chip technologies below 2 nanometers  
Expanding BASF’s Kuanyin site with a strengthened Innovation Center and advanced quality analysis capabilities  
Strengthening supply chain resilience and enhancing customer support in Taiwan and beyond  
Taipei – October 20, 2026 – BASF today signed a Letter of Intent (LOI) with Taiwan’s Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), underscoring its long-term commitment to supporting the growth of Taiwan’s semiconductor ecosystem. Through this investment, BASF’s Electronic Materials business is expanding its Kuanyin site in Taoyuan with additional production capacity for advanced semiconductor materials, enhanced quality analysis capabilities, and an expanded Innovation Center. The investment is designed to support increasing global demand for leading-edge semiconductor manufacturing technologies, including advanced nodes below 2 nanometers, while strengthening supply chain resilience and customer proximity.
“Taiwan is a global hub for semiconductor innovation and manufacturing, with leading-edge process technologies and a highly integrated industry ecosystem. Setting the strategic base for BASF’s global Electronic Materials operations in Taiwan in 2025 reflected the strategic importance of Taiwan within the global semiconductor ecosystem and reinforced our confidence in the market’s long-term growth potential,” said Gops Pillay, President, Global Operating Division of BASF.
As the semiconductor industry progresses toward process nodes below 2 nanometers, demand for advanced, high-purity specialty chemical formulations continues to rise. Through the expansion of its Kuanyin site, BASF will strengthen its Innovation Center and broaden its technical and analytical capabilities for leading-edge semiconductor technologies supporting the AI era. The investment will deepen collaboration with key industry partners, enabling the joint development of next-generation materials while reinforcing Taiwan’s position as a global semiconductor innovation hub.
The investment will further strengthen BASF’s local manufacturing, quality assurance and technical service capabilities in Taiwan, enabling the company to provide customers with a more reliable supply of advanced semiconductor materials, faster technical support, and closer collaboration. At the same time, it will enhance supply chain resilience and reinforce BASF’s role as a trusted long-term partner to the semiconductor industry.
“The signing of this Letter of Intent marks another important milestone in BASF’s long-term commitment to the semiconductor industry,” said Jens Liebermann, Senior Vice President, Global Electronic Materials business and Chairman of BASF Taiwan. “As semiconductor technologies continue to advance, innovation in materials must keep pace with our customers’ evolving needs. By strengthening our local manufacturing, innovation, and technical service capabilities, we are deepening collaboration with our customers and accelerating the development of materials solutions for future technology generations, while further enhancing supply chain resilience.”
As a trusted materials partner to the global semiconductor industry, BASF’s Electronic Materials business has maintained a strong presence in Taiwan for more than two decades. The business provides high-performance process chemicals and customized formulation solutions for the advanced semiconductor and display industry as well as specialized metal systems for consumer electronics applications. 
 
About BASF’s Dispersions & Resins division  
The Dispersions & Resins division of BASF develops, produces and markets a range of high-quality polymer dispersions, resins, additives and electronic materials worldwide. These raw materials are used in formulations for several industries, including coatings, construction, adhesives, printing and packaging, electronics and paper. With its comprehensive product portfolio and extensive knowledge of the industry, the Dispersions & Resins division offers its customers innovative and sustainable solutions and helps them advance their formulations. For further information about the Dispersions & Resins division, please visit  www.dispersions-resins.basf.com 
 
About BASF 
At BASF, we create chemistry for a sustainable future. Our ambition: We want to be the preferred chemical company to enable our customers’ green transformation. We combine economic success with environmental protection and social responsibility. Around 95,000 employees in the BASF Group contribute to the success of our customers in nearly all sectors and almost every country in the world. Our portfolio comprises, as core businesses, the segments Chemicals, Materials, Industrial Solutions, and Nutrition & Care; our standalone businesses are bundled in the segments Surface Technologies and Agricultural Solutions. BASF generated sales of around €60 billion in 2025. BASF shares are traded on the stock exchange in Frankfurt (BAS) and as American Depositary Receipts (BASFY) in the United States. Further information at  www.basf.com

Strategic and operational highlights
The following are recently announced highlights:

3M introduced Cooling Film technology for fleet and rail applications , expanding its portfolio of thermal management solutions for transportation customers. Applied to vehicle roofs, the highly reflective performance film uses thermal management technology to reduce heat buildup and help keep interiors noticeably cooler.
3M showcased how its materials science expertise supports innovation in golf equipment through its collaboration with PING . By pairing PING's expertise in club design and custom manufacturing with 3M's broad portfolio of materials science solutions, the two companies can collaborate on engineering solutions that turn complex technical challenges into repeatable, high-quality results on the course.

title: 3M announces collaboration with GSEO to advance Expanded Beam Optical manufacturing and development
content_text:
3M announces collaboration with GSEO to advance Expanded Beam Optical manufacturing and development
Oct 19, 2026 • 5:31 PM EDT 
Download as PDF
ST. PAUL, Minn. , Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- 3M (NYSE: MMM) today announced a collaboration with Genius Electronic Optical Co., Ltd.  (GSEO, Taiwan: 3406), an optical technology company, to advance technology development and manufacturing for 3M's Expanded Beam Optical (EBO) solutions. In support of these efforts, 3M expects to make a strategic investment to acquire approximately 4.7% of GSEO's common shares as part of the company's private placement of newly issued shares, subject to customary closing conditions.
The collaboration brings together 3M's EBO technology leadership, optical interconnect expertise, materials science, manufacturing scale and customer relationships with GSEO's precision optics manufacturing capabilities and production scale. Together, the companies aim to support EBO commercialization and long-term capacity expansion to meet growing demand from hyperscale data centers and other advanced connectivity applications.
"3M is investing in capabilities and partnerships that can accelerate innovation for our customers," said William Brown, 3M Chairman and CEO. "By selecting GSEO as a manufacturing partner and investing in the company, we are strengthening the path to scale next-generation optical connectivity solutions for high-performance data center infrastructure."
GSEO's existing precision optics manufacturing capabilities and technical development experience are expected to support manufacturing readiness for 3M's EBO ferrules, co-packaged optics solutions and related optical interconnect applications. The collaboration is part of 3M's broader EBO ecosystem strategy, which includes continued work with customers and partners across the optical interconnect market.
"GSEO is pleased to expand its relationship with 3M as we work together to advance optical interconnect solutions for next-generation data center infrastructure," said Micro Kuo, GSEO CEO and President. "This collaboration brings together complementary technology and manufacturing strengths to support continued innovation and help meet the performance demands of high-growth connectivity markets."
3M expects the strategic investment to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to customary closing conditions.

title: Infineon signs 200-millimeter silicon carbide wafer supply agreement with Wolfspeed to further strengthen supply chain resilience Business & Financial Press Oct 15, 2026
content_text:
Infineon signs 200-millimeter silicon carbide wafer supply agreement with Wolfspeed to further strengthen supply chain resilience 
Business & Financial Press
Oct 15, 2026 
Multi-year agreement with Wolfspeed supports Infineon’s conversion from 150-millimeter to 200-millimeter silicon carbide (SiC) manufacturing 
Expanded substrate sourcing strengthens supply chain resilience and enhances flexibility to support future growth 
Agreement supports growing demand for SiC power semiconductors for electric vehicles, renewable energy systems and AI datacenter power infrastructure 
Munich, Germany and Durham, N.C – 15 October 2026 – Infineon Technologies AG (FSE: IFX / OTCQX: IFNNY) and Wolfspeed, Inc. (NYSE: WOLF) have signed a new multi-year supply agreement for 200-millimeter silicon carbide (SiC) wafers, transitioning Infineon's existing Wolfspeed supply relationship from 150-millimeter to 200-millimeter substrate technology. SiC semiconductors have become a key enabling technology for the electrification and energy efficiency applications that drive global decarbonization, from electric vehicles and renewable energy systems to AI datacenter power infrastructure. The agreement directly supports Infineon's conversion to 200-millimeter SiC manufacturing, strengthening Infineon's position as the global leader in power semiconductors and reinforcing the supply chain resilience that underpins its SiC growth strategy.
“Silicon carbide is at the heart of the energy transition, and securing a high-quality, resilient supply of 200-millimeter substrates is essential to delivering on our customers’ long-term commitments,” said Alexander Gorski, Chief Operations Officer at Infineon. “This agreement further broadens our strong supply base for our 200-millimeter high-volume manufacturing, building on a 20-year supply relationship between our two companies. It strengthens supply chain security for our customers and provides additional flexibility and scalability to support Infineon's future growth.”
AI datacenters are beginning to emerge as a significant demand driver for SiC power semiconductors. Power conversion efficiency across the datacenter power chain is a direct operating cost consideration for hyperscalers managing infrastructure at scale. The switching efficiency and thermal performance of SiC make it a technically suitable option for specific power conversion stages where silicon reaches its practical limits. Together with growing SiC adoption across electric vehicle drivetrains, solar inverters and industrial motor drives, these trends support a strong long-term outlook for high-quality 200-millimeter SiC substrates. 
The transition to 200-millimeter SiC wafers delivers large manufacturing economics compared to 150-millimeter production. Larger wafer diameter increases usable die area per wafer, reduces per-unit substrate cost, and improves overall manufacturing efficiency. Infineon operates a multi-source SiC substrate strategy to maintain supply chain flexibility and quality across its global manufacturing network, including its world-class 200-millimeter SiC fab in Kulim, Malaysia, which is designed to be the world’s largest and most competitive silicon carbide manufacturing facility.
About Infineon
Infineon Technologies AG is a global semiconductor leader in power systems and IoT. Infineon drives decarbonization and digitalization with its products and solutions. The Company had around 57,000 employees worldwide (end of September 2025) and generated revenue of about €14.7 billion in the 2025 fiscal year (ending 30 September). Infineon is listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange (ticker symbol: IFX) and in the USA on the OTCQX International over-the-counter market (ticker symbol: IFNNY).

title: onsemi and Sungrow Advance Utility-Scale Energy Storage Performance with SiC Hybrid Technology
content_text:
onsemi and Sungrow Advance Utility-Scale Energy Storage Performance with SiC Hybrid Technology
October 14, 2026 at 6:01 AM EDT
PDF Version 
Advanced EliteSiC hybrid technology maximizes usable energy as electricity demand surges
Summary 
As AI-driven electricity demand accelerates worldwide, utilities and energy providers are under growing pressure to store and deliver energy more efficiently. Battery energy storage system (BESS) providers are seeking advanced power conversion technologies to improve performance and system economics. To address these needs, Sungrow has adopted onsemi’s latest SiC hybrid power module technology for its PowerTitan 3.0 energy storage platform. The design improves system efficiency, helping utilities and energy providers increase usable energy output while lowering operating costs.
News Highlights 
onsemi’s EliteSiC hybrid power module enables the highest-density battery energy storage system deployments, helping energy providers meet growing electricity demand from AI, renewable energy and electrification
New BESS architecture improves inverter-level efficiency by 0.4%, helping maximize energy delivered to the grid while reducing losses and improving reliability
Sungrow’s PowerTitan 3.0 energy storage platform integrates onsemi’s latest EliteSiC hybrid power module technology, optimized for high-power DC-AC energy conversion in utility-scale battery storage applications
SCOTTSDALE, Ariz., Oct. 14, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- onsemi (Nasdaq: ON) today announced that Sungrow, a global leader in renewable energy technology, has adopted onsemi’s latest EliteSiC silicon carbide (SiC) hybrid power module technology for the Sungrow PowerTitan 3.0 energy storage platform. The integration enables improved efficiency and enhanced system performance for utility-scale battery energy storage systems (BESS).
Helping Sungrow Deliver More Usable Energy 
The PowerTitan 3.0 platform incorporates onsemi’s high-density power integrated modules (PIMs) , optimized for advanced three-level inverter architectures used in high-power energy storage applications.
Compared with the previous-generation platform, the new architecture improves inverter-level efficiency by 0.4%, enabling higher-power battery storage deployments without sacrificing efficiency. The architecture supports power conversion units rated up to 450 kW, contributing to the platform’s increased power density and higher-power deployment capability.
With the performance advantages of SiC , the solution supports key system-level benefits including:
Peak efficiency exceeding 99.3% to reduce energy loss in utility-scale systems
Increased power density supports higher-power BESS deployments
Enhanced thermal performance supports reliable operation in high-power applications
Improved system economics through a hybrid SiC design optimized for large-scale deployment
The design win builds on a long-standing strategic relationship between onsemi and Sungrow. Through extensive engineering and validation activities, the companies collaborated throughout platform definition, system optimization and qualification to meet the demanding performance requirements of next-generation energy storage deployments.
“PowerTitan 3.0 represents Sungrow’s continued innovation in advanced energy storage system design,” said Chen Peng, General Manager of Energy Storage Conversion Product Line at Sungrow Energy Storage Business Unit. “By integrating advanced technologies and collaborating with strategic partners such as onsemi, Sungrow is accelerating the deployment of higher-performance storage solutions that deliver greater value throughout the lifecycle of energy assets. With growing market recognition, Sungrow estimates delivering 10 GWh of PowerTitan 3.0 across Europe in 2026, further supporting the region’s transition toward a more flexible and resilient energy system.”
“At utility scale, even small improvements in power conversion efficiency can have a meaningful impact on battery energy storage system (BESS) performance and total cost of ownership,” said Sergio Fissore, Vice President and General Manager, IPD Power Division, onsemi. “Our EliteSiC hybrid power module enables higher-efficiency, higher-density energy storage systems that help maximize usable energy and improve system reliability. Together with Sungrow, we're advancing the power conversion technologies needed to support the next generation of energy infrastructure.”
Why Fractions of a Percent Matter 
At utility scale, even small efficiency improvements can generate meaningful financial and environmental benefits. According to onsemi analysis, a 0.4% efficiency improvement delivered by the new SiC hybrid module could save more than 475 MWh of energy annually in a 100 MW battery energy storage installation compared with the previous-generation module.
Those energy savings can help reduce operating costs, increase usable energy delivered to customers and lower overall emissions. The architecture also enables higher overload capability and improved thermal performance, helping customers extract more usable energy from every storage asset.
Supporting the Infrastructure Behind the AI Era 
Utilities and energy providers are seeking ways to store more energy, reduce conversion losses and improve overall system economics to meet unprecedented demand amid the AI infrastructure buildout and electrification transition.
Industry forecasts project the battery energy storage market will more than double by 2030 as utilities invest in infrastructure needed to support increasing electricity demand and renewable energy deployment. At the same time, energy storage providers are moving toward higher-power, higher-voltage architectures to improve system economics.

Full-year 2026 total net sales expected to be between €44 billion and €45 billion, with a gross margin around 56% 
VELDHOVEN, the Netherlands, October 14, 2026 – Today, ASML Holding NV (ASML) has published its 2026 third-quarter results. 
Q3 total net sales of €11.7 billion, gross margin of 57.5%, net income of €5.0 billion

End-quarter cash and cash equivalents and short-term investments 7,582 12,735 
Numbers have been rounded for readers' convenience. A complete summary of US GAAP Consolidated Statements of Operations is published on www.asml.com.
CEO statement and outlook 
"In the third quarter we reported a record total net sales of €11.7 billion, towards the high end of our guidance, reflecting the strong execution of our ramp-up. Installed Base Management sales 1 came in above guidance at €3.3 billion as a result of the continued strong demand for productivity upgrades. This drove the gross margin above guidance at 57.5%.
"Our customers continue to increase their short- and medium-term equipment demand forecasts with us, driven primarily by their views on the size and duration of AI-related investments. In light of their demand visibility, some customers are expressing an interest in placing orders with us for 2029 and even 2030. 
"With such strong visibility and an order book momentum that continues to increase quarter on quarter this year, we now expect that our supply as currently planned for both 2027 and 2028 will not fully meet the demand of our customers 2 . Given this, we are investigating ways to increase capacity for 2028 beyond the 30% increase we previously communicated. In addition, we continue to provide significant wafer capacity to our customers through our productivity upgrade portfolio.
"We expect fourth-quarter 2026 total net sales between €14.2 billion and €15.2 billion, with a gross margin around 57%. We expect R&D costs of around €1.2 billion and SG&A costs of around €0.4 billion. We expect total net sales for 2026 to be between €44 billion and €45 billion, with a gross margin around 56%," said ASML President and Chief Executive Officer Christophe Fouquet.
Update share buyback program and dividend 
In the third quarter, we purchased around €4.1 billion worth of shares under the current 2026–2028 share buyback program.
An interim dividend over 2026 of €1.88 per ordinary share will be made payable on November 4, 2026.
Details of the share buyback program as well as transactions pursuant thereto, and details of the dividend are published on ASML's website (www.asml.com/investors).

title: Applied Materials Set to Outperform as AI Drives Sustained Demand for Wafer Fab Equipment
content_text:
Applied Materials Set to Outperform as AI Drives Sustained Demand for Wafer Fab Equipment
Oct 13, 2026 at 12:45 PM EDT
PDF Version 
Company expects strong multi-year growth as global AI infrastructure buildout fuels demand for leading-edge foundry-logic, DRAM and advanced packaging – areas where Applied has built market leadership 
Expects wafer fab equipment (WFE) spending to grow faster through 2030 than over the past decade; targets more than 2 percentage points of WFE share gain from calendar 2025 to 2030 
Targets higher profitability through 2030 with non-GAAP gross margin target of approximately 54 percent and non-GAAP operating margin target of approximately 40 percent 
Committed to distribute 80 to 100 percent of free cash flow to shareholders over time 
SAN FRANCISCO , Oct. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- At its 2026 SEMICON West Investor Breakfast Presentation held today, Applied Materials, Inc. presented its longer-term growth expectations and outlined how its leadership in materials engineering positions the company to outperform the wafer fab equipment (WFE) market over the coming years.
“The global buildout of AI infrastructure is driving a new era of growth for wafer fab equipment,” said Gary Dickerson , President and CEO of Applied Materials. “Applied Materials has built leadership in the fastest growing areas of the market that have the greatest impact on AI computing performance, power efficiency and cost, and our advanced services offerings enable chipmakers to increase yield and fab output. Our industry-leading capabilities position Applied for continued growth and outperformance in the years ahead.”
The race for AI computing leadership requires tremendous technology innovation and capacity expansion to support infrastructure scaling, which is fueling sustained WFE investments – bigger than any of the industry’s past growth drivers. The growth and diversity of AI applications from generative to agentic and physical AI require increasing amounts of silicon. Applied expects leading-edge foundry-logic, DRAM and advanced packaging to drive around 75 percent of WFE growth from 2025-2030. Applied has strong number-one process equipment positions in all three areas and is targeting to gain more than 2 percentage points of WFE market share from calendar 2025 to 2030.
To support the industry’s capacity expansion, Applied is utilizing its unique eBeam technology and advanced service solutions to help chipmakers accelerate the ramp of new process nodes and optimize yield, output and cost in high-volume manufacturing. With the industry’s highest resolution and fastest imaging capabilities, Applied’s eBeam equipment portfolio is expected to generate $2 billion in revenue in calendar year 2026. The company is expecting service revenue to grow more than 20 percent this calendar year and to exceed $12 billion in revenue by calendar year 2030, representing a mid-teens compound annual growth rate.
“For the past 10 years, Applied Materials has been making strategic investments to build the industry’s most enabling portfolio for AI computing,” said Brice Hill , Senior Vice President and CFO. “As AI drives wafer fab equipment growth, we are focused on further increasing profitability and operating leverage while investing in R&D programs that will fuel our outperformance into the future.”
Based on the company’s expectations for semiconductor industry growth, Applied is investing to more than double its R&D lab and manufacturing capacity from current levels by 2030. The company yesterday unveiled its new Equipment and Process Innovation and Commercialization (EPIC) Center in Silicon Valley , the world’s largest facility dedicated to collaborative semiconductor process technology and manufacturing equipment R&D. To date, Applied has announced 15 EPIC Center partnerships with leading chipmakers, systems companies, equipment partners and universities. Applied has also recently expanded its manufacturing infrastructure in Austin, Texas , Singapore and Treviso, Italy .
Non-GAAP Financial Measures 
Forward-looking non-GAAP gross margin and non-GAAP operating margin targets for 2030 assume non-GAAP adjustments as applicable for future periods, which we are unable to predict without unreasonable efforts due to their inherent uncertainty. Free cash flow is a non-GAAP measure and is defined as net cash provided by operating activities less capital expenditures. Management uses non-GAAP financial measures to evaluate the company’s operating and financial performance and for planning purposes, and as performance measures in its executive compensation program. Applied believes these measures enhance an overall understanding of its performance and investors’ ability to review the company’s business from the same perspective as the company’s management, and facilitate comparisons of results with prior periods on a consistent basis by excluding items that management does not believe are indicative of Applied’s ongoing operating performance. There are limitations in using non-GAAP financial measures because the non-GAAP financial measures are not prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, may be different from non-GAAP financial measures used by other companies, and may exclude certain items that may have a material impact upon our reported financial results.
Forward-Looking Statements 
This press release contains forward-looking statements, including those regarding anticipated growth and trends in our businesses and markets, industry outlooks and demand drivers, technology transitions, our business and financial performance and market share positions, our capital allocation and cash deployment strategies, our investment and growth strategies, our development of new products and technologies, the plans and expectations for the EPIC Center, our business outlook, expectations for our financial performance for calendar year 2026, our business and financial targets for 2030, and other statements that are not historical facts. The partners aim to convert discarded foam into recycled polyols and amines for use in new polyurethane products.
content_text:
Evonik, Toyotsu Chemiplas and Sanyo Chemical launch polyurethane recycling initiative in Japan
Collaboration combines expertise in collection, logistics, and chemical recycling
Initiative targets recovery of polyols and amines from post-consumer polyurethane foam and production scrap
Partners will evaluate the process, with the aim of commercializing the recycling model in Japan
Evonik has partnered with Toyotsu Chemiplas Corporation and Sanyo Chemical Industries, Ltd. to develop a recycling model for polyurethane foam in Japan for Japan. The partners aim to convert discarded foam into recycled polyols and amines for use in new polyurethane products. The initiative forms part of Evonik’s wider efforts to scale  polyurethane recycling through collaboration across the value chain.
Polyurethane foam is widely used in everyday products, including automotive seats, mattresses, and furniture. However, used foam is frequently incinerated or sent to landfill, while conventional mechanical recycling generally restricts its use to lower-value applications. Chemical recycling offers the potential to recover important raw materials, such as polyols and amines, and thereby help close the loop in flexible polyurethane foam production.
Polyurethane foam made with 100% recycled polyol using Evonik's chemical recycling process 
Within the partnership, Toyotsu Chemiplas will coordinate the initiative and contribute its collection network and logistics expertise. Sanyo Chemical will provide its expertise in polyol development and process technology, while Evonik will contribute its proprietary hydrolysis-based chemical recycling process and technical expertise.
Evonik's pilot plant for PU recycling in Hanau, Germany 
“This collaboration with our Japanese partners represents an important step toward developing a practical recycling model for polyurethane foam in Japan. It also reflects Evonik’s ambition to scale polyurethane recycling by building strong partnerships across the value chain. By combining local collection and logistics expertise with polyol development and our chemical recycling technology, we aim to recover valuable raw materials for use in new, high-quality polyurethane foams and support more circular polyurethane value chains,” said Dr. Martin Trocha, Head of Comfort & Adhesives in Evonik’s business line Interface & Polyurethane Additives.
The partners plan to develop a system for collecting both post-consumer polyurethane foam and post-industrial scrap. The collected material will be chemically recycled into high-purity polyols and amines, intended for reuse as raw materials in the manufacture of new polyurethane products.
Proposed recycling model for polyurethane foam in Japan
The hydrolysis-based chemical recycling process from Evonik is designed to produce recycled polyols with high purity and consistent quality. The process provides polyurethane foam manufacturers with a drop-in solution and can significantly reduce carbon footprint compared to virgin materials. New polyurethane foam has already been successfully produced using 100 percent recycled polyol derived from the process.
The three companies will jointly evaluate the entire process, from collection and sorting to the production of recycled polyols and the manufacture of new polyurethane products. This work will include quality assessments and further updates to Evonik’s existing life cycle assessment to reflect the proposed value chain in Japan. The objective is to commercialize the technology and establish a scalable recycling model for polyurethane foam in Japan.
About the partnership
Toyotsu Chemiplas is responsible for coordinating the initiative and will contribute its collection network and logistics expertise. Sanyo Chemical will contribute its expertise in polyol development and process technology. Evonik will provide its hydrolysis chemical recycling technology and technical expertise as part of its global efforts to support the scale-up of polyurethane recycling through partnerships.
Further information:
Polyurethane recycling at Evonik 
Evonik's Interface & Polyurethane Additives business line 
Evonik: Leading beyond chemistry
Evonik goes beyond the boundaries of chemistry with its combination of innovative strength and leading technological expertise. The global chemical company, headquartered in Essen, Germany, is active in more than 100 countries and generated sales of €14.1 billion and earnings (adjusted EBITDA) of €1.9 billion in 2025. The common motivation of the approximately 31,000 employees: to provide customers with a decisive competitive advantage with tailor-made products and solutions as a superforce for industry, thereby improving people's lives. In all markets. Every day.
About Custom Solutions
The Custom Solutions segment focuses on innovation-driven, tailor-made solutions for customers in specific growth markets. These solutions include additives for coatings, adhesives and sealants, polyurethane foams and lubricants, catalysts, and ingredients for the cosmetics, cleaning and pharmaceutical industries. In 2025, the segment generated sales of €5.4 billion with around 9,500 employees.

title: Applied Materials Unveils $5 Billion EPIC Center in Silicon Valley to Accelerate Semiconductor Innovation for the AI Era
content_text:
Applied Materials Unveils $5 Billion EPIC Center in Silicon Valley to Accelerate Semiconductor Innovation for the AI Era
Oct 12, 2026 at 4:30 PM EDT
PDF Version 
$5 billion  investment creates the world’s largest semiconductor equipment and process technology R&D facility 
Purpose-built to accelerate the path from breakthrough innovation to high-volume manufacturing of next-generation chipmaking technologies 
Leading chipmakers, systems companies, equipment partners and research universities have committed to develop inside EPIC 
 
SUNNYVALE, Calif. ,  Oct. 12, 2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) --  Applied Materials, Inc. , the leader in materials engineering for the semiconductor industry, today unveiled its Equipment and Process Innovation and Commercialization (EPIC) Center, a  $5 billion  capital investment* to build the world’s largest facility dedicated to collaborative semiconductor process technology and manufacturing equipment R&D. Inside the EPIC Center, leading chipmakers, systems companies, equipment partners and university researchers will work side by side with Applied’s scientists and engineers to accelerate the pace of chip innovation for the AI era.
“As AI infrastructure scales, the demands of high-performance computing are driving unprecedented complexity across the chipmaking roadmap,” said  Gary Dickerson , President and CEO of Applied Materials. “To win the race for AI leadership, our industry must rethink and re-engineer how we collaborate to develop and commercialize the next generation of semiconductor technologies. At EPIC, the world’s leading chipmakers, system designers, equipment partners and researchers will work side by side with our teams to accelerate the path from breakthrough materials innovation to high-volume manufacturing faster than ever before.”
Purpose-Built to Accelerate Innovation and Commercialization 
Unveiled today at Applied’s  Sunnyvale, California , campus, the EPIC Center represents one of the most complex R&D construction projects in the world. The 600,000-square-foot structure houses nearly four acres of advanced cleanroom space and required more than six million construction hours to complete. Its foundation holds enough concrete to fill 34 Olympic-sized swimming pools, and its steel-reinforced structure holds enough steel to build two  Eiffel Towers . Thirty-four roof trusses cover the cleanrooms, each spanning nearly 300 feet in length and weighing as much as 12 school buses.
EPIC is designed to reinvent the R&D model the industry has relied on for decades. In the traditional model, foundational materials research happens in one environment, equipment and process development in another, and process integration and pilot production in a third, with a careful handoff at every phase. The EPIC Center is designed to remove these handoffs, putting the people who invent the materials, build the equipment, and make the chips together in a state-of-the-art facility purpose-built for commercialization.
EPIC is founded on a simple conviction: the technologies the AI era demands are too complex and too consequential for any one company to invent alone. The EPIC Center opens with a founding roster that spans the AI technology stack. Founding partners TSMC, Intel, SK hynix, Micron and Samsung Electronics are joined by innovation partners Broadcom, Advantest, SCREEN, KIOXIA, and Besi; and by research partners  Arizona State University ,  Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute ,  Stanford University ,  UC Berkeley , and  UCLA Samueli School of Engineering . Each partner brings its own roadmap challenges and engineers into the facility, working in tight, secure learning cycles alongside Applied teams. Over time, additional companies and organizations are expected to join the EPIC ecosystem.
Leaders from many of the EPIC Center partner companies attended the unveiling event, getting a first glimpse inside the facility. The day started with a summit hosted by Dr.  Prabu Raja , President of the  Semiconductor Products Group  at Applied Materials, where R&D leaders from top semiconductor design, manufacturing and equipment companies discussed key challenges facing growth and progress in the global chip industry.
“Materials innovation has outgrown serial development – at today’s atomic-scale dimensions, many materials and materials interfaces behave in entirely new ways, and making them work at industry scale demands coordinated development and integrated solutions,” said Dr.  Prabu Raja . “EPIC is the only place where materials, process technology and equipment will be innovated in parallel, which increases the success rate of new materials and technologies. Because our customers’ own engineers help optimize the technology before it ever reaches their factory, what leaves EPIC arrives at the fab ready to ramp to high performance and high yield sooner.”
Applied expects the EPIC operating model to deliver returns on both sides of the partnerships. Chipmakers gain earliest access to next-generation materials and equipment, shorter learning cycles and a faster path to volume production. Applied gains visibility across several generations of emerging technology challenges, informing where the company directs its R&D investments to create value for customers and have its systems and services designed in.
Supporting Quotes from Industry and Academic Leaders 
“For three decades, TSMC and Applied Materials have grown together – pushing the boundaries of semiconductor technology through every major transition. Thirty years ago, the leading-edge production node was 350 nanometers. Today, it is 2 nanometers. Working hand-in-hand with the industry, we have shrunk features 175-fold. As chipmaking complexity grows exponentially, our partnership is more vital than ever. Beyond 2nm, collaborating with Applied gives us early access to the disruptive equipment technologies that define the future. This fast-tracks the leap from R&D to high-volume manufacturing for the energy-efficient AI architectures of tomorrow – including new architecture, low-resistance wiring, and advanced packaging. We are proud to be a founding partner of EPIC, accelerating the innovations that will power AI from the data center to the edge.” – Dr.  C.C. Wei , Chairman and CEO of TSMC 
“AI is creating a multi-trillion-dollar opportunity for the semiconductor industry. To capture it, we need continued innovation in transistors, interconnects and advanced packaging. At Intel, we see a path to more than a trillion transistors in a package by 2030. As architectures become more complex and R&D costs continue to rise, we need to move faster and work more closely with our equipment partners. EPIC gives our teams the opportunity to work side by side with Applied on materials and process innovation – helping us accelerate development, improve R&D efficiency and bring new technologies to market faster.” –  Lip-Bu Tan , CEO, Intel 
“Data-intensive AI workloads are driving massive demand for high-performance memory and storage, and innovation in materials and process technology is a critical enabler of next-generation memory. As a founding partner of EPIC, Micron will work side by side with Applied Materials to accelerate innovation and bring next-generation memory technologies from research to high-volume manufacturing at scale.” –  Sanjay Mehrotra , Chairman and CEO, Micron Technology 
“The defining challenge of AI computing is moving data fast enough to keep increasingly powerful processors fully utilized, and meeting that challenge requires memory with far greater bandwidth, speed and capacity. At EPIC, SK hynix and Applied will bring together our leadership in advanced memory with Applied’s leadership in materials engineering and semiconductor manufacturing technology to address major inflections across HBM, DRAM and NAND, and accelerate memory innovation for the AI era.” – Nohjung Kwak, President and CEO of SK hynix 
“Samsung takes an end-to-end view of AI-era computing – across leading-edge logic, memory and advanced packaging. Applied Materials brings uniquely broad process equipment leadership across all three domains, and at EPIC together we will develop, iterate and deploy breakthrough technologies faster than ever, at the pace AI scaling demands.” – Jaihyuk Song, Chief Technology Officer (CTO) of Device Solutions Division, Samsung Electronics 
“The next frontier of AI will be defined by how seamlessly the industry can integrate vast amounts of compute, memory and connectivity into high-performance systems, and that depends on breakthrough advances in advanced packaging. As an innovation partner at EPIC, Broadcom can engage earlier with Applied’s foundational technologies and manufacturing capabilities, connecting future system requirements to the packaging innovations needed to realize them and accelerating the path from concept to commercialization.” –  Charlie Kawwas , Ph.D., President of  Semiconductor Solutions Group , Broadcom 
“Future performance improvements will depend on advanced 3D architectures and heterogeneous integration. As these technologies converge, it becomes increasingly important to connect insights from front-end process development with those from back-end test and measurement. EPIC breaks down these traditional barriers by bringing together Applied Materials’ leadership in materials engineering and process control with Advantest's leadership in semiconductor test and measurement, including capabilities enabled through the Advantest Innovation Center. Together, we are helping the world’s leading semiconductor manufacturers improve yield, accelerate production ramps, and bring next-generation AI systems to market faster.” –  Doug Lefever , Representative Director and Group CEO, Advantest Corporation 
“At EPIC, we have a unique opportunity to co-optimize the critical wet and dry processes behind next-generation chip architectures. We can together accelerate the innovations required to master increasingly complex 3D devices and advanced packaging structures. By driving tighter process integration with materials engineering, we can help chipmakers unlock higher yields, faster production ramps, and the manufacturing scale required for the AI future.” –  Masato Goto , President and CEO, SCREEN Holdings Co., Ltd. 
“AI is making the world increasingly data-driven, and future breakthroughs will depend on memory, logic, and interconnect technologies working seamlessly within integrated systems. We believe the EPIC Center provides a powerful platform for collaboration across technology domains. By working closely with Applied Materials engineers and other partners, we can accelerate the development of next-generation memory technologies.” –  Hideshi Miyajima , Ph.D., Managing Executive Officer and Chief Technology Officer,  KIOXIA Corporation 
“The future of AI depends not only on more powerful chips, but on the chip-to-chip interconnects that drive performance, bandwidth and power efficiency. Besi and Applied recognized early that hybrid bonding would be foundational to next-generation AI systems, and by combining Besi’s leadership in precision die-to-wafer bonding with Applied’s leadership in front-end processing, we are advancing hybrid bonding technology to enable future high-performance 3D integrated devices. EPIC extends that model of high-velocity co-innovation across the ecosystem, accelerating the technologies that will shape future AI systems.” –  Richard Blickman , President and CEO, BE Semiconductor Industries (Besi) 
“ASU has developed a very strong working relationship with Applied Materials through the Materials-to-Fab Center at  ASU Research Park , and we are excited to dig deeper into this partnership at the EPIC Center, where researchers, engineers and manufacturers converge to accelerate bold ideas from the lab to breakthroughs in the fab. EPIC will also serve as a cornerstone for the semiconductor talent pipeline and by working alongside Applied’s scientists and engineers, our students will gain the systems-level perspective needed to drive the future of AI innovation.” –  Michael Crow , President,  Arizona State University 
“UC Berkeley has helped shape microelectronics from its earliest days, advancing the research and talent that continue to propel the semiconductor industry, and our collaboration with Applied Materials is a great example of how academia and industry must work together to meet the scale and opportunity of what’s ahead. The EPIC platform gives our researchers access to the same cutting-edge capabilities used by the world’s leading chipmakers, within a manufacturing-relevant environment, so ideas can be tested, refined and transformed much faster into the semiconductor breakthroughs that will advance the frontier of AI.” –  Rich Lyons , Chancellor,  UC Berkeley 
“Many of the technologies powering today’s AI revolution began in university labs years, often decades, before they transformed the world. As computing demand increases, we must accelerate the pace at which new semiconductor materials, devices and integration technologies move from discovery to deployment. As an inaugural research partner at the EPIC Center, RPI’s students and researchers gain access to world-class experts and a direct pathway to test and validate academic advances in real-world production environments – a powerful blueprint for high-velocity industry-academia collaboration in the AI era.” –  Martin Schmidt , President of RPI 
“The explosive growth of AI is pushing semiconductor technology researchers to find new ways to increase energy efficiency of semiconductor chips. Opportunities abound in discovering new materials and inventing new devices. Experimentation demands faster cycles of innovation and closer collaboration across the ecosystem. Beyond the existing broad research engagement between  Stanford  faculty and Applied Materials, the EPIC Center presents an additional opportunity that enables our students and researchers to engage directly with industry-scale tools and experts, accelerating discovery while gaining the industry-relevant experience needed to lead future advances in semiconductor manufacturing.” –  H.S. Philip Wong , Willard R. and  Inez Kerr Bell Professor  in the  School of Engineering ,  Stanford University 
“Accelerating semiconductor innovation in the new era of AI requires transformative collaboration between universities and industry partners more than ever before. UCLA has a long history of pioneering semiconductor research and innovation, and our collaboration with Applied Materials at the EPIC Center builds on that legacy by bringing together university research and industry expertise to advance the chip technologies that will define the future of computing while preparing the next generation of engineers.” – Ah-Hyung “Alissa” Park, Ronald and  Valerie Sugar Dean  of UCLA Samueli 
*Capital spending is expected to scale over time to approximately $5 billion as customer projects commence.

This press release contains forward-looking statements, including those regarding Applied’s investment and growth strategies, the development of new materials and technologies, industry outlook and technology requirements, the plans and expectations for the EPIC Center, and other statements that are not historical facts. These statements and their underlying assumptions are subject to risks and uncertainties and are not guarantees of future performance. Factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied by such statements include, without limitation: the demand for semiconductors and customers’ technology requirements; the ability to develop new and innovative technologies; the ability to obtain and protect intellectual property rights in key technologies; the ability to achieve the objectives of the EPIC Center; and other risks and uncertainties described in Applied’s filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission, including Applied’s most recent Forms 10-K, 10-Q and 8-K. All forward-looking statements are based on management’s current estimates, projections and assumptions, and Applied assumes no obligation to update them.
About the EPIC Center 
The EPIC Center (Equipment and Process Innovation and Commercialization) is Applied Materials’ flagship R&D facility in Silicon Valley, designed to compress the timeline from early-stage materials research to high-volume semiconductor manufacturing. By bringing chipmakers, equipment partners and university researchers into the same building as Applied’s scientists and engineers, EPIC enables parallel rather than sequential development of materials, equipment and process technology, shortening learning cycles and accelerating the commercialization of the innovations that will power the AI era. title: Applied Materials and UCLA Engineering Accelerate Semiconductor Innovation at the EPIC Center
content_text:
Applied Materials and UCLA Engineering Accelerate Semiconductor Innovation at the EPIC Center
Oct 8, 2026 at 4:05 PM EDT
PDF Version 
R&D programs to focus on speeding up the commercialization pipeline so chip technology moves from breakthrough research to full-scale manufacturing faster 
Collaborative work at the state-of-the-art facility in Silicon Valley pairs UCLA’s semiconductor research strength with Applied’s cutting-edge chipmaking equipment and process integration expertise 
SANTA CLARA, Calif. , Oct. 08, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Applied Materials, Inc. today announced that the UCLA Samueli School of Engineering will join the company’s EPIC Center in Silicon Valley as a research partner. Together with Applied’s scientists and engineers, UCLA researchers will work to solve semiconductor materials and integration challenges with a focus on shortening the time it takes to bring breakthrough research to commercialization.
“As the industry races to bring new AI chip technologies to market, the EPIC Center will play a pivotal role by convening the industry’s top innovators in a collaborative environment designed to accelerate the path from breakthrough research to full-scale manufacturing,” said Dr. Prabu Raja , President of the Semiconductor Products Group at Applied Materials. “UCLA has a long history of semiconductor technology innovation and Applied looks forward to welcoming their researchers to the EPIC Center where together we will work to solve the industry’s toughest challenges.”
The EPIC Center aims to accelerate chip R&D by bridging the gap between traditional academic innovation and industrial-scale development. UCLA researchers will have access to advanced chipmaking tools so that new ideas can be validated and tested in a commercial fab environment, thereby shortening the path from concept to production.
UCLA Samueli brings extensive expertise across semiconductor devices, materials, electronics and computing. In 1991, Henry Samueli co-founded Broadcom Corporation while teaching at UCLA . The school is also home to the Center for Heterogeneous Integration and Performance Scaling (CHIPS) Lab , which brings together researchers across disciplines to advance semiconductor technologies and address challenges in chip design, manufacturing and integration.
By collaborating at the EPIC Center, Applied Materials and UCLA will focus R&D programs on the semiconductor industry’s most critical challenges in areas including 3D chip scaling, advanced packaging and the discovery of new materials for improving energy-efficient AI compute performance. The work will complement and extend the efforts of UCLA’s Semiconductor Hub , which Applied joined as a co-founding member earlier this year. Applied’s ongoing commitment to strengthen the ties between industry and academia is aimed at empowering the next generation of engineers and researchers to bring semiconductor breakthroughs to market faster.
“Accelerating semiconductor innovation in the new era of AI requires transformative collaboration between universities and industry partners more than ever before,” said Ah-Hyung “Alissa” Park, Ronald and Valerie Sugar Dean of UCLA Samueli. “UCLA has a long history of pioneering semiconductor research and innovation, and this collaboration builds on that legacy by bringing together university research and industry expertise to advance the chip technologies that will define the future of computing while preparing the next generation of engineers.”
Applied’s new EPIC (Equipment and Process Innovation and Commercialization) Center in Silicon Valley represents the largest-ever U.S . investment in advanced semiconductor equipment R&D. The center is designed from the ground up to dramatically reduce the time it takes to commercialize breakthrough technologies from early-stage research to full-scale manufacturing. The facility is on track to become operational in 2026. Visit the EPIC Center website to learn more.

title: TOPPAN to Participate in ‘Rapidus CORE’ Global Ecosystem Framework
content_text:
TOPPAN to Participate in ‘Rapidus CORE’ Global Ecosystem Framework
Offering input on cutting-edge semiconductors as a Design Solution Associate to contribute to LSI design and development
Tweet 
Tokyo – October 8, 2026 – TOPPAN Inc. (TOPPAN), a TOPPAN Group company and wholly owned subsidiary of TOPPAN Holdings Inc. (TYO: 7911), will participate as a Design Solution Associate in the Rapidus Collaborative Open Rapid Ecosystem (Rapidus CORE)—a global ecosystem framework for the development and mass production of cutting-edge semiconductors to be established by Rapidus Corporation (Rapidus).
Background & Objectives
In recent years, driven by the rapid growth of AI, high-performance computing, and automated driving technologies, global demand has surged for cutting-edge logic semiconductors that deliver both exceptional processing power and high energy efficiency. Consequently, semiconductor manufacturing processes are transitioning to next-generation nodes, starting with the 2 nm generation. However, as process miniaturization advances, Large-Scale Integration (LSI) design has become extraordinarily complex. Increased risks in manufacturing lead to costly redesigns and heavier verification workloads, driving up development costs and lengthening time-to-market. Addressing these challenges requires advanced design solutions that seamlessly bridge design and manufacturing, alongside open collaborative frameworks.
To drive innovation across the entire semiconductor value chain—from design to front-end and back-end processes—and to accelerate next-generation LSI development by creating partner-driven value beyond traditional supply chain boundaries, Rapidus has launched Rapidus CORE, a global ecosystem framework.
As part of the initial rollout of Rapidus CORE, Rapidus announced Design Solution Associates, a group of design-related companies in which TOPPAN will participate. Design Solution Associates connect customers with Rapidus, providing specialized engineering resources and technical expertise to facilitate the rapid launch of semiconductor development. This collaborative model strengthens support systems from design through manufacturing tailored to diverse customer needs.
Some of TOPPAN’s core strengths are its expertise built over many years in LSI design technology and the optimization of Electronic Design Automation (EDA) environments. In particular, TOPPAN possesses extensive technical know-how in complex design solutions required for advanced process nodes, including low-power design, timing closure addressing Process, Voltage, Temperature (PVT) variations, and high-speed interface implementation.
By joining Rapidus CORE as a Design Solution Associate, TOPPAN will offer end-to-end support for Rapidus customers—from initial specification analysis to circuit design, layout, and physical verification. In doing so, TOPPAN will help significantly reduce the design complexity, cost, and risks associated with cutting-edge process nodes, contributing to establishing a sustainable semiconductor ecosystem.
Future Goals
In addition to contributing to establishing a sustainable ecosystem for next-generation semiconductors, through participation in Rapidus CORE, TOPPAN will contribute to creating new value as well as resolving societal issues by leveraging cutting-edge semiconductor technology.
About the TOPPAN Group
Established in Tokyo in 1900, the TOPPAN Group is a leading and diversified global provider committed to delivering sustainable, integrated solutions in fields including printing, communications, security, packaging, décor materials, electronics, and digital transformation. The TOPPAN Group’s global team of more than 50,000 employees offers optimal solutions enabled by industry-leading expertise and technologies to address the diverse challenges of every business sector and society and contribute to the achievement of shared sustainability goals.

title: AVerMedia and Stereolabs Accelerate AI Vision Deployment with NVIDIA JetPack 7.2
content_text:
AVerMedia and Stereolabs Accelerate AI Vision Deployment with NVIDIA JetPack 7.2
Content Import
Wed, 10/07/2026 - 07:00
AVerMedia and Stereolabs Accelerate AI Vision Deployment with NVIDIA JetPack 7.2
October 7, 2026
General
Unified integration delivers faster time to market, broad camera compatibility, and more efficient use of memory across Jetson Orin and Thor modules
TAIPEI, Taiwan & PARIS--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 7, 2026-- AVerMedia Technologies, Inc. and Stereolabs , an Ouster company, today announced NVIDIA JetPack 7.2 support across all Stereolabs ZED X GMSL cameras and AVerMedia’s NVIDIA Jetson carrier boards, offering robotics and edge AI developers a faster and more efficient path from development to production.
This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261007896664/en/
AVerMedia and Stereolabs Accelerate AI Vision Deployment with NVIDIA JetPack 7.2
The collaboration combines AVerMedia’s NVIDIA Jetson carrier-board and Board Support Package (BSP) engineering expertise with Stereolabs’ unified ZED X driver architecture. With this approach, AVerMedia can adapt the hardware-specific device tree and generate drivers for the JetPack and Jetson Linux versions required by customers, reducing the repeated exchanges previously required for each hardware or software update.
This collaboration allows AVerMedia hardware development and Stereolabs software releases to progress in parallel, shortening validation cycles and giving customers greater control over product schedules.
The unified workflow allows Stereolabs to focus on camera firmware, ISP performance, and ZED SDK capabilities, while AVerMedia manages the carrier-board-specific integration and validation required for production deployment.
More AI Capability from Available Jetson Memory
Memory is a critical resource in embedded AI systems, particularly when multiple camera streams, perception models, and robotics applications must run simultaneously on a single Jetson module.
NVIDIA JetPack 7.2 introduces Jetson agent skills that help developers optimize memory usage across the software stack. These agent-driven workflows can tune bootloader carveouts, optimize kernel memory reservations, streamline user-space services, and improve inference memory usage. These optimizations free up critical memory for vision processing and AI workloads, enabling richer applications on smaller memory footprints and lowering total cost of ownership.
Key Customer Benefits:
Faster time to market: Hardware modifications and software releases can be integrated and validated more efficiently.
Broad compatibility: NVIDIA JetPack 7.2 supports all Stereolabs cameras across AVerMedia’s NVIDIA Jetson carrier-board portfolio, including Jetson Orin and Jetson Thor platforms.
More efficient memory utilization: Developers can make more memory available for camera processing, AI models, and robotics applications.
Greater software control: Reproducible Debian packages provide traceability of the driver, device tree, installation flow, and kernel code used in production.
Simplified lifecycle management: Drivers can be regenerated for required JetPack and Linux versions, supporting long-term maintenance, compliance, and product updates.
“By anchoring the platform-specific integration work with AVerMedia, where we’re doubling down on both companies’ hardware expertise, both teams can develop in parallel and respond to customer requirements more quickly,” said Ihsane Debbache , VP of Engineering at Stereolabs. “This integration gives developers a more efficient path to deploying Stereolabs ZED vision across AVerMedia Jetson platforms.”
NVIDIA JetPack 7.2 also provides official Yocto support, giving developers greater control over reproducible, production-ready software images for Jetson Orin and Jetson Thor platforms.
“Customers need both faster integration and more efficient use of their computing resources,” said Alex Liu , Vice President of AVerMedia. “By combining Stereolabs’ vision technology and AVerMedia’s BSP and hardware engineering expertise, we can help customers reduce integration risk, make better use of available Jetson memory, and deploy more capable AI vision systems faster.”
Ongoing support and transition to NVIDIA JetPack 7.2 will be available through AVerMedia support form .
About AVerMedia Technologies, Inc.
AVerMedia Technologies, Inc. is a leading global provider of application-ready Edge AI turnkey solutions, recognized for its expertise in video and audio technologies. AVerMedia offers customized, fully integrated hardware and software solutions designed to accelerate AI deployments across various industries, including smart cities, robotics, and industrial automation. AVerMedia is dedicated to delivering cutting-edge AI inference solutions that enable businesses to scale AI effectively and reliably at the edge.
About Stereolabs
Stereolabs , a wholly owned subsidiary of Ouster, Inc. (Nasdaq: OUST), is a leader of 3D vision and depth perception for Physical AI. Its ZED camera family and ZED SDK platform provide real-time depth sensing, spatial mapping, and AI-powered object understanding for robotics, industrial automation, and smart spaces.

title: Infineon and ZuriQ deepen partnership to advance scalable quantum chips Business & Financial Press Oct 07, 2026
content_text:
Infineon and ZuriQ deepen partnership to advance scalable quantum chips
Business & Financial Press
Oct 07, 2026 
Expanding partnership targets the next generation of trapped-ion quantum computing 
Infineon and ZuriQ build on recent technology progress to scale quantum processing units toward commercial systems 
Partners combine Infineon's semiconductor manufacturing expertise with ZuriQ's innovative and highly scalable Penning micro-trap architecture 
Munich, Germany / Zurich, Switzerland – 7 October 2026 – Infineon Technologies AG (FSE: IFX / OTCQX: IFNNY) and ZuriQ AG, a Swiss quantum computing company spun out of ETH Zurich, today announced the expansion of their collaboration to advance scalable quantum computing hardware. The partnership combines ZuriQ’s pioneering trapped-ion quantum computing architecture with Infineon’s expertise in semiconductor manufacturing, advanced packaging, and integrated photonics.
Previous development work by ZuriQ and Infineon demonstrated the feasibility of this novel architecture by trapping a 3×3 array of nine individually controlled ions, achieving the largest two-dimensional array of its kind to date. The next step in the partnership is to scale the technology to significantly larger qubit counts. ZuriQ’s quantum innovation and Infineon’s industrial-scale semiconductor manufacturing expertise will jointly advance the development of next-generation quantum computing systems.
“Advancing quantum computing toward commercial impact will require close collaboration between quantum innovators and industrial technology leaders,” said Pavel Hrmo, co-founder and CEO of ZuriQ. “Through our collaboration with Infineon, which possesses a deep understanding of process development and semiconductor technologies, we are turning ZuriQ’s technological progress into scalable, manufacturable quantum hardware. This partnership brings us closer to developing quantum computing technologies for real-world applications.”
“Progress in quantum computing requires breakthroughs in physics, but also robust manufacturing technologies capable of supporting the development of future large-scale systems,” said Clemens Rössler, Senior Director and Head of Quantum Processing Units at Infineon. “With our expertise in semiconductor manufacturing, integration and advanced packaging, we are enabling the next generation of trapped-ion quantum processing units. By combining our semiconductor competence with ZuriQ’s design and architecture expertise, we are taking an important step toward industrializing this key technology.”
Unlike conventional trapped-ion quantum computers that use one-dimensional ion chains, ZuriQ has developed a natively two-dimensional Penning micro-trap architecture that uses electric and magnetic fields to move ions directly across the chip. The design avoids complex junction structures, making it easier to accommodate larger qubit arrays. Integrating this approach with Infineon’s advanced photonics and semiconductor processes is central to accelerating the transition from laboratory demonstration to real-world applications.
Two-dimensional trapped-ion technology offers a promising path toward precise, scalable quantum processors for fault-tolerant quantum computing and commercial applications. Quantum computers have the potential to solve highly complex problems beyond the capabilities of conventional computers and supercomputers.
This collaboration between an innovative quantum computing start-up and a global semiconductor leader enhances Europe’s quantum ecosystem and strengthens Europe’s position in this strategically important area. Further advances in this field are expected to accelerate innovation across high-impact sectors such as medicine, logistics, materials science, and artificial intelligence, helping solve some of the world’s most complex computational challenges.
About ZuriQ 
Founded in 2024, ZuriQ AG is a Swiss-based quantum computing company and ETH Zurich spin-off. By developing a novel trapped-ion architecture based on static electromagnetic fields, ZuriQ aims to overcome key scalability challenges in quantum computing. The company focuses on high-fidelity quantum operations, rapid qubit scaling, and reconfigurable quantum systems, paving the way toward commercially relevant quantum applications.
About Infineon
Infineon Technologies AG is a global semiconductor leader in power systems and IoT. Infineon drives decarbonization and digitalization with its products and solutions. The Company had around 57,000 employees worldwide (end of September 2025) and generated revenue of about €14.7 billion in the 2025 fiscal year (ending 30 September). Infineon is listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange (ticker symbol: IFX) and in the USA on the OTCQX International over-the-counter market (ticker symbol: IFNNY).

title: Press Releases Group Air Liquide has successfully issued a 2 billion euros multi-tranche bond October 06, 2026
source: Air Liquide - Press Releases & News / Press Releases / News
content_text:
Air Liquide has successfully issued a 2 billion euros multi-tranche bond
Paris, France, 
October 06, 2026 
Press Releases
Group
Following the Capital Markets Day held on October 5, and the announcement of the BEYOND new strategic plan, Air Liquide has successfully issued a new 2 billion euros multi-tranche bond. After diversifying its funding sources through a bond issuance on the Swiss market in the first quarter of the year, this transaction marks Air Liquide’s return to the Euro market. 
The net proceeds of this issuance will be used by Air Liquide for the financing of the Group’s general corporate purposes as well as the refinancing of its debt. 
This transaction, very significantly oversubscribed by investors, was executed under the Group's Euro Medium Term Note (EMTN) programme. With this issuance, Air Liquide is raising 2 billion euros with 2-year, 5-year and 10-year maturities. Taking into consideration the pre-hedging arrangements, the weighted average interest rate is below 4.00% per annum. 
This issue will be rated « A » by Standard & Poor’s and Scope Ratings and « A2 » by Moody’s. 
Jérôme Pelletan, Chief Financial Officer and Member of the Air Liquide Executive Committee, stated: 
“This new issuance, executed in a complex environment, reflects investor confidence in the implementation of our new BEYOND strategic plan for 2030. The funds raised will support our capital allocation and drive the development of our activities in future growth markets.”
