title: Applied Materials and Intel Collaborate to Accelerate Chipmaking Innovations for AI-Driven Computing
content_text:
Applied Materials and Intel Collaborate to Accelerate Chipmaking Innovations for AI-Driven Computing
Oct 6, 2026 at 9:00 AM EDT
PDF Version 
Collaborations at Applied’s EPIC Center in Silicon Valley and Intel’s R&D campus in Oregon aim to develop breakthroughs in next-generation transistors, interconnects and advanced packaging technologies for AI chips and systems 
Collaboration builds on the companies’ long history of working together to solve complex semiconductor device scaling challenges 
SANTA CLARA, Calif. , Oct. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Applied Materials, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMAT), the leader in materials engineering for the semiconductor industry, today announced it is working with Intel Corporation (Nasdaq: INTC) to accelerate development of chipmaking innovations for next-generation transistors, interconnects and advanced packaging technologies. The collaboration will bring together cutting-edge capabilities from Applied’s EPIC Center in Silicon Valley and Intel’s R&D campus in Hillsboro, Oregon to shorten time-to-market of advanced semiconductor technologies essential to AI computing.
“Applied and Intel share a decades-long history of deep collaboration focused on pushing the boundaries of materials engineering to advance the semiconductor roadmap,” said Gary Dickerson , President and CEO of Applied Materials. “Bringing our teams together at the EPIC Center will deepen that partnership and accelerate the transistor, interconnect and packaging innovations needed to drive the future of AI computing.”
“The demand for AI computing is driving the need for major advances in performance, power efficiency, and packaging. Intel is focused on delivering those innovations and doing it in close collaboration with partners across the ecosystem,” said Lip-Bu Tan , CEO of Intel . “Applied Materials is an important partner, and we look forward to expanding our work together at the EPIC Center to help accelerate the path from the lab to high-volume manufacturing in the United States.”
Teams from Applied Materials and Intel are collaborating on next-generation materials, process technologies and device architectures for advanced logic nodes targeting AI workloads, and will continue this work at the EPIC Center. The collaboration spans both front-end and back-end-of-line advancements, including interconnect scaling. The collaboration also involves development of advanced packaging technologies for Foveros-based 3D stacking, supporting higher interconnect density, improved power delivery, and enhanced thermal performance for high-performance compute platforms designed to accelerate emerging agentic AI workloads.
“With the chipmaking roadmap becoming more complex at each process node, accelerating innovations in semiconductor devices, interconnects and packaging requires deeper collaboration across R&D and manufacturing,” said Dr. Prabu Raja , President of the Semiconductor Products Group at Applied Materials. “We look forward to working closely with Intel as a founding partner of the EPIC Center to shorten development cycles and bring new technologies to market faster.”
“Accelerating our R&D to keep pace with the rapid buildout of AI infrastructure is critical to delivering the technology, manufacturing excellence and foundry services our customers expect from Intel Foundry,” said Naga Chandrasekaran, Executive Vice President, Chief Technology and Operations Officer and General Manager of Intel Foundry. “Applied Materials’ new EPIC Center provides an environment where our teams can collaborate even more closely and at higher velocity to accelerate materials development and process innovations.”
Applied’s new EPIC (Equipment and Process Innovation and Commercialization) Center in Silicon Valley , which is scheduled to be operationally ready this year, is designed from the ground up to dramatically reduce the time it takes to commercialize breakthrough technologies from early-stage research to full-scale manufacturing. For chipmakers, the EPIC Center will provide earlier access to Applied’s R&D portfolio, faster cycles of learning and accelerated transfer of next-generation technologies into high-volume manufacturing, within a secure collaborative environment. In addition, the co-innovation programs at the EPIC Center will provide Applied with greater multi-node visibility to guide R&D investments while increasing R&D productivity and value sharing.
Forward-Looking Statements 
This press release contains forward-looking statements, including those regarding Applied’s investment and growth strategies, the development of new materials and technologies, industry outlook and technology requirements, the plans and expectations for the EPIC Center, and other statements that are not historical facts. These statements and their underlying assumptions are subject to risks and uncertainties and are not guarantees of future performance. Factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied by such statements include, without limitation: the demand for semiconductors and customers’ technology requirements; the ability to develop new and innovative technologies; the ability to obtain and protect intellectual property rights in key technologies; the ability to achieve the objectives of the EPIC Center; and other risks and uncertainties described in Applied’s filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission, including Applied’s most recent Forms 10-K, 10-Q and 8-K. All forward-looking statements are based on management’s current estimates, projections and assumptions, and Applied assumes no obligation to update them.

title: Oct. 6, 2026 Business & Products Sumitomo Chemical Achieves Production-Scale Manufacturing of Liquid Crystal Polymer (LCP) Using Biomass Feedstock in Preparation for Mass Production The Company Will Begin Supplying Samples Produced Through Biomanufacturing
source: Sumitomo Chemical - News Releases Filter / Press Releases
content_text:
News Releases 
Business & Products 
Sumitomo Chemical Achieves Production-Scale Manufacturing of Liquid Crystal Polymer (LCP) Using Biomass Feedstock in Preparation for Mass ProductionThe Company Will Begin Supplying Samples Produced Through Biomanufacturing 
News Releases
Sumitomo Chemical Achieves Production-Scale Manufacturing of Liquid Crystal Polymer (LCP) Using Biomass Feedstock in Preparation for Mass Production
The Company Will Begin Supplying Samples Produced Through Biomanufacturing 
Oct. 6, 2026
Sumitomo Chemical has achieved production-scale manufacturing of liquid crystal polymer (LCP) that contains a portion of monomer derived from biomass feedstock (bio-based LCP (*1) ). As a global supplier in the LCP market, the Company is preparing a mass production system for bio-based LCP leveraging biomanufacturing technology. It also plans to begin providing customers with samples obtained from this production-scale manufacturing.
LCP is a type of super engineering plastic that offers excellent heat resistance and flame retardancy. Its outstanding fluidity, in particular, makes it well-suited to a wide range of applications, from electronic devices such as smartphones to automotive components and office automation equipment. While most of the raw materials used to produce LCP have traditionally been derived from fossil resources, there is growing demand for shifting to biomass feedstock and reducing the carbon footprint (*2) in order to achieve a sustainable society.
In response to rising customer demand, Sumitomo Chemical has been advancing the development of bio-based LCP. In June 2025, the Company established technology to mass-produce the material and has since been advancing studies to scale up this technology. It has now confirmed through production-scale manufacturing that it can produce LCP partially containing biomass-derived monomers at a quality equivalent to that of LCP made with conventional fossil-based feedstock (*3) .
The manufacturing process to produce the bio-based LCP used by Sumitomo Chemical adopts a segregation approach, in which biomass feedstock and non-biomass feedstock are kept completely separate from each other during production. This makes it possible to clearly quantify the amount of biomass feedstock included in the final product. There is also another approach, known as mass balance, in which biomass feedstock and non-biomass feedstock are mixed together, and the characteristics of the biomass feedstock are allocated to part of the product output in proportion to the amount of biomass feedstock used. Sumitomo Chemical will assess the characteristics of each approach to utilize a method that best meets customer needs.
As part of its long-term vision, Sumitomo Chemical has positioned itself as a company that solves social issues through innovative technologies. In its biomanufacturing, the Company is pursuing the hybridization of chemical and biological technologies.
In the green bio (*4) field, Sumitomo Chemical is working toward the achievement of a regenerative society through both chemical crop protection products and biorationals (*5) . In the red bio (*4) field, it is contributing to human health through pharmaceutical development, CDMO (*6) services based on cell culture technologies, and regenerative medicine and cell therapy. In the white bio (*4) and gray bio (*4) fields, it is promoting sustainable manufacturing through the utilization of biomass-derived feedstock with organic synthesis technologies and omics technologies (*7) .
Going forward, Sumitomo Chemical will continue to create value by leveraging chemical technologies and biotechnology, and contribute to solving society's challenges by providing innovative solutions.
(*1) An LCP produced using a principal raw material, a biomass derived monomer made from 100% biomass feedstock. The portion of the biomass-derived content of the bio-based LCP equivalent to our existing compounding grade, SUMIKASUPER E6008, is approximately 30% based on raw material weight. 
(*2) A measurement of the total greenhouse gas emissions released during each stage of a product’s life cycle—from raw material procurement to manufacturing, use, and disposal—expressed in terms of the equivalent CO₂ emissions. 
(*3) Based on an internal evaluation carried out by Sumitomo Chemical in accordance with ASTM International standards, the Company confirmed that, from the perspective of heat resistance, fluidity, and the mechanical properties of the material—the key characteristics that represent the advantages of LCP— LCP that contains a portion of monomer derived from biomass feedstock (bio-based LCP) is equivalent in quality to LCP made with conventional fossil-based feedstock. 
(*4) Terms used to classify, by color, the fields in which biotechnology is applied: green for food and agriculture, red for medicine, white for industry and energy, and gray for the environment. 
(*5) Microbial crop protection products derived from natural sources, plant growth regulators and rhizosphere microbial products, and solutions that use these products to protect crops from pests and diseases or improve crop quality and yield. 
(*6) CDMO is an acronym of Contract Development and Manufacturing Organization, a business that undertakes process development and manufacturing for customers. 
(*7) Technologies that comprehensively analyze biological molecules such as genes, proteins, and metabolites.

title: Proterial and FEV Jointly Validate xEV Traction Motor Concept Using Amorphous Alloy and High-Performance Heavy-Rare-Earth-Free Magnet Technology Simulation Study Indicates Potential for Higher Efficiency, Increased Output, and Reduced Weight
source: Hitachi Metals - Proterial 2026 Press Releases / Press Releases
content_text:
TOP 
News Release 
2026 
Proterial and FEV Jointly Validate xEV Traction Motor Concept Using Amorphous Alloy and High-Performance Heavy-Rare-Earth-Free Magnet Technology Simulation Study Indicates Potential for Higher Efficiency, Increased Output, and Reduced Weight 
R&D 
Proterial and FEV Jointly Validate xEV Traction Motor Concept Using Amorphous Alloy and High-Performance Heavy-Rare-Earth-Free Magnet Technology
Simulation Study Indicates Potential for Higher Efficiency, Increased Output, and Reduced Weight
October 5, 2026 
Proterial, Ltd.
FEV
Proterial, Ltd. (“Proterial”), a leading manufacturer of advanced materials and components, and FEV, a global engineering and consulting partner for mobility, energy, and software, have jointly investigated and validated an electrified-vehicle (xEV) traction motor concept that combines Proterial’s amorphous alloy technology with its high-performance heavy-rare-earth (HRE) -free neodymium sintered magnet technology. Bringing together Proterial’s advanced materials expertise and FEV’s capabilities in electric drive design, simulation, benchmarking, and system-level evaluation, the partners developed and assessed a traction motor concept designed to make full use of the characteristics of these materials. Simulation results indicate the potential to improve motor efficiency while simultaneously increasing output and reducing weight compared with a defined 230-kW-class reference motor. The study also highlights the potential to reduce resource and procurement risks associated with HREs. Proterial and FEV will continue exploring how advanced material technologies can be translated into tangible benefits at the traction motor and complete drive-system level. 
The results of this study will be jointly presented by FEV and Proterial at the Aachen Automotive Colloquium, to be held in Aachen, Germany, from October 5 to 7, 2026. 
1. Background
As the mobility industry continues to pursue decarbonization and improved energy efficiency, demand is increasing for traction motors and drive systems with lower power consumption, higher performance, and reduced reliance on critical raw materials. In electrified vehicles (xEVs), improving efficiency supports lower electricity consumption and longer driving range; in other applications, such as heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) equipment, data centers, electric vertical takeoff and advanced air mobility, exemplified by eVTOL aircraft, and robotics, higher-efficiency electric motors can help reduce overall energy demand. Amorphous alloy is attracting attention because it can reduce motor losses. Compared with conventional electrical steel sheets commonly used in electric motor cores, amorphous alloy offers lower iron loss. For neodymium magnets used in xEV traction motors, there is also strong demand to reduce dependence on HREs, which face resource constraints, and to mitigate procurement risk. To address these market needs, Proterial has developed continuous lamination and bonding technology for amorphous alloy ribbon suitable for punching into motor cores, as well as high-performance HRE-free neodymium sintered magnets that can be applied to xEV traction motors. Proterial established the Motor Solutions Department within its Marketing & Sales Division in November 2025 and is promoting initiatives to verify the value of its products from the perspective of traction motors and complete drive systems, and to develop optimized solutions for customer applications rather than individual products alone.
2. Overview and Results of the Study
As part of these initiatives undertaken by its Motor Solutions Department, Proterial is working with FEV, with project promotion support from Beyond Materials Corporation, to evaluate the application of amorphous alloy and HRE-free magnet technology to xEV traction motors.
In this study, FEV established a reference motor model for a 230 kW drive unit, representative of modern passenger-car battery electric vehicle (BEV) applications, using silicon steel sheets for the motor core. The effect of applying amorphous alloy was then evaluated through electromagnetic simulation. Rather than simply replacing the motor core material, the partners examined a traction motor concept that reflects current trends in electric drive systems, including inverter and reduction gears, while making best use of the low-iron-loss characteristics of amorphous alloy, due to an increased maximum motor speed. The reduction ratio of the transmission was adjusted so that the maximum torque and speed during vehicle operation would be equivalent to that of the reference drive unit (Table 1). The study also applied Proterial’s high-performance HRE-free neodymium sintered magnet, which combines high magnetic performance, due to a high remanence flux density, and strong resistance to demagnetization, due to a high coercivity, without relying on HREs. Compared with the reference, the simulation results indicate the potential to improve motor efficiency while simultaneously increasing output to 300 kW and reducing weight by 27 % (Table 1).

3. Future Outlook
Proterial and FEV intend to continue exploring how advanced material technologies can be translated into measurable benefits in electric motors and complete drive systems. Through its Motor Solutions Department and in collaboration with its business divisions, Proterial will continue to verify material value from the perspective of customer applications and propose optimized solutions. FEV will contribute its engineering, simulation, benchmarking, and system-integration expertise to assess how new materials can support next-generation electric drive concepts. Together, the partners aim to support higher-efficiency electric mobility and other emerging applications, including eVTOLs and humanoid robots, while contributing to a more sustainable society.
4. Presentation at the Aachen Automotive Colloquium
The results of this joint study will be presented by FEV and Proterial at the Aachen Automotive Colloquium, to be held in Aachen, Germany, from October 5 to 7, 2026. A mock-up of the traction motor structure examined in this study will also be on display at FEV's Booth No. 9.

About Proterial
Headquartered in Tokyo, Japan, Proterial is a leading manufacturer of advanced materials, primarily metal-based materials.
In the motor field, the company’s business divisions collaborate under the leadership of the Motor Solutions Department to serve as development partners for customers. Proterial verifies the value of materials from the perspective of motors and complete drive systems and proposes optimal solutions.
As a manufacturer capable of providing a comprehensive range of motor materials, Proterial will continue to contribute to lower electricity consumption in xEVs and reduced power consumption in air-conditioning and data-center equipment through the application of its products to high-efficiency motors. The company will also contribute to a sustainable society by providing solutions for emerging applications, including eVTOLs and humanoid robots.
About FEV
FEV is a global engineering and consulting partner for mobility, energy and software. Since 1978, FEV has been developing innovative technologies and solutions across the entire product lifecycle – from strategy and concept development through engineering and validation to implementation, optimization and support. Combining engineering expertise with software, digital technologies and AI, FEV helps its customers develop sustainable technologies, intelligent systems and future-oriented solutions. With around 5,600 employees at more than 45 locations worldwide, FEV serves customers across a wide range of industries.
About Beyond Materials
Beyond Materials is a joint venture established by Mitsubishi Corporation and FEV Consulting GmbH. By combining the two companies’ expertise in the materials industry, global networks, insights into customer needs across industries such as automotive, energy, and robotics, and capabilities in end-product design and development, Beyond Materials provides consulting and engineering-related solutions to companies throughout the materials industry and its value chain. Its services include market and technology research, strategy development, product development, and proof-of-concept testing.

Notes and Terms
Note: The numerical values described in this document are simulation results based on specified conditions and are not guaranteed product values.
xEV: A general term for electrified vehicles, including battery electric vehicles (BEVs), hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs), plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEVs), and related vehicles.
eVTOL: A next-generation aircraft capable of vertical takeoff and landing using electric power (electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft).
Amorphous alloy: A metallic material with no crystalline structure, obtained by rapidly cooling a molten alloy.
Reference Model: The reference model values include nominal values.
WLTP Class 3: An international standard driving cycle applied to typical passenger vehicles, simulating real-world driving conditions from urban roads to highways.
ARTEMIS MW 150 Drive Cycle: One of the driving patterns developed under Europe’s ARTEMIS (Assessment and Reliability of Transport Emission Models and Inventory Systems) project; it is widely used to evaluate fuel consumption, electricity consumption, emissions, and motor efficiency.
Heavy rare earths: Rare-earth elements with relatively high atomic weights, such as terbium (Tb) and dysprosium (Dy).
Remanence B r and coercivity H cJ : Key magnetic properties of permanent magnets. Remanence indicates magnetic flux density retained after magnetization, while coercivity indicates resistance to demagnetization.

title: onsemi and Synaptics Announce Revised Merger Agreement
content_text:
onsemi and Synaptics Announce Revised Merger Agreement
October 1, 2026 at 4:34 PM EDT
PDF Version 
Revised Terms to Deliver Higher onsemi Shareholder Value through Immediate EPS Accretion 
Amended Agreement Follows Thorough Review of Unsolicited Competing Proposal 
SCOTTSDALE, Ariz. and SAN JOSE, Calif., Oct. 01, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- onsemi (NASDAQ: ON) and Synaptics Incorporated (NASDAQ: SYNA) ("Synaptics") today announced they have amended their June 25, 2026 merger agreement. The amendment follows an unsolicited competing proposal received from a third party.
Under the revised agreement, onsemi will acquire Synaptics for $123 per share in cash for an aggregate value of approximately $5.7 billion as compared to approximately $7 billion for the prior agreement. The transaction is expected to be immediately accretive to onsemi’s non-GAAP earnings per share and provides value certainty for Synaptics’ shareholders.
“As was the case when we initially announced the acquisition, Synaptics addresses an important aspect of our strategic direction, and we believe the revised merger agreement represents a more financially attractive transaction for our shareholders,” said Hassane El-Khoury, President and CEO of onsemi. “The all-cash transaction delivers higher value to our shareholders through lower total cost consideration, and we now expect the transaction to be immediately accretive to non-GAAP EPS upon closing. In addition, we have identified incremental opportunities to create shareholder value beyond the previously announced $200 million of annual run-rate synergies. These additional benefits from revenue synergies and insourcing of a portion of Synaptics’ production are expected to be realized after the initial 18 months post-close, further strengthening the long-term earnings and cash flow profile of the combined company.”
El-Khoury continued, “Synaptics is accretive to our long-term model, with a strong growth outlook and attractive gross margin profile that will help accelerate onsemi’s evolution. Additionally, Synaptics complements growth in our AI data center business, and brings to onsemi its highly profitable human-machine interface, and sensing products businesses that generate strong and predictable cash flows, providing the combined company with a durable funding engine to accelerate its connected compute capabilities.”
After careful review with its financial and legal advisors, the Synaptics Board unanimously determined that the onsemi transaction, as amended, continues to be in the best interests of Synaptics and its shareholders.
"Our Board has been singularly focused on delivering the best outcome for our shareholders, and today's amended agreement reflects that commitment," said Rahul Patel, Synaptics President and CEO. “By transitioning to an all-cash structure, we are providing value certainty at a meaningful premium as compared to current value. We are confident this path is the right choice for our shareholders."
The transaction will be financed through a combination of cash on hand and committed financing. onsemi has obtained fully committed debt financing from Morgan Stanley. The amended merger agreement does not include a closing condition related to onsemi’s financing.
The transaction is still expected to close by mid-2027, subject to approval by Synaptics shareholders, the receipt of required regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions. The transaction has been approved by the United States Federal Trade Commission, and regulators in other jurisdictions are reviewing the transaction.

onsemi (Nasdaq: ON) delivers intelligent power and sensing technologies that enable electrification, energy efficiency, safety, and automation across automotive, industrial, and AI data center end-markets. With a highly differentiated and innovative product portfolio, onsemi helps customers solve complex challenges to achieve higher efficiency, improved performance, and lower system cost, while supporting a safer, cleaner, and more energy-efficient world. Synaptics (Nasdaq: SYNA) is driving innovation in AI at the Edge, bringing AI closer to end users and transforming how we engage with intelligent connected devices, whether at home, at work, or on the move. As a go-to partner for forward-thinking product innovators, Synaptics powers the future with its cutting-edge Synaptics Astra™ AI-Native embedded compute, wireless connectivity, and multimodal sensing solutions. We’re making the digital experience smarter, faster, more intuitive, secure, and seamless. title: Applied Materials and Besi Expand Strategic Partnership to Advance Next-Generation Packaging for AI Scaling
source: Applied Materials - Investor News Releases / Press Releases
content_text:
Applied Materials and Besi Expand Strategic Partnership to Advance Next-Generation Packaging for AI Scaling
Oct 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM EDT
PDF Version 
Besi joins Applied's EPIC Center as an Innovation Partner, extending a collaboration that began in 2020 with the companies' joint Hybrid Bonding Center of Excellence in Singapore 
Expanded collaboration targets next-generation 3D IC scaling, logic and memory integration, and photonics applications supporting AI infrastructure build-out 
Partnership expands beyond die-to-wafer hybrid bonding to new hybrid bonding platforms, scaling of thermo-compression bonding (TCB), and new die-on-wafer, die-on-die and die-on-panel architectures 
SANTA CLARA, Calif. and DUIVEN, The Netherlands , Oct. 01, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Applied Materials, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMAT) and BE Semiconductor Industries N.V. (Besi) ( Euronext Amsterdam : BESI) today announced an expansion of their longstanding strategic partnership, with Besi joining Applied's EPIC Center as an Innovation Partner. The collaboration builds on the companies’ joint development program launched in 2020 and extends co-innovation beyond hybrid bonding into new interconnect architectures and applications supporting the semiconductor industry's AI-driven scaling roadmap.
As the AI infrastructure build-out drives demand for higher-density, higher-bandwidth chip-to-chip and chip-to-package interconnects, the expanded partnership is intended to give mutual customers earlier access to co-optimized process and assembly solutions spanning the full advanced packaging flow – from wafer-level hybrid bonding through panel-scale integration.
In 2020, Applied and Besi established a joint Center of Excellence at Applied's Advanced Packaging Development Center in Singapore , combining Applied's process expertise in etch, planarization, deposition, wafer cleaning, metrology, inspection and particle defect control with Besi's die placement, interconnect and assembly technology. That collaboration resulted in Kinex™ , the industry’s first integrated die-to-wafer hybrid bonding system.
“Besi has been a trusted partner since we began co-developing next-generation hybrid bonding solutions,” said Gary Dickerson , President and CEO of Applied Materials. “With Besi joining EPIC as an Innovation Partner, we’re extending that collaboration across the interconnect technologies our customers need to scale AI systems. Bringing this work into Applied's EPIC Center gives both companies earlier visibility into where the roadmap is headed and lets us co-optimize the full packaging flow.”
“Our center of excellence with Applied in Singapore has been foundational to Besi's hybrid bonding roadmap,” said Richard Blickman , CEO and Chairman of the Board of Management of Besi. “Joining Applied's EPIC Center as an Innovation Partner is a natural next step, giving us a seat alongside the leading logic, memory and systems companies as we advance TCB scaling, die-on-panel integration and the interconnect technologies that will define the next generation of AI and photonics systems”
As an Innovation Partner, Besi engineers will work alongside Applied's teams at the EPIC Center to accelerate joint development across a broader set of interconnect and integration technologies. While advanced packaging was historically treated as a back-end assembly step, technologies such as hybrid bonding and panel-level integration now depend on the same materials engineering disciplines that define front-end wafer fabrication.
“Advanced packaging is no longer a back-end assembly step – it is a materials engineering challenge that demands the same precision and cleanliness as front-end wafer fabrication,” said Dr. Prabu Raja , President of the Semiconductor Products Group at Applied Materials. “Developing these technologies together with Besi engineers in a front-end R&D environment like the EPIC Center will allow us to treat them as one connected flow rather than a series of isolated steps. That gives our mutual customers earlier access to co-optimized solutions and a faster path from development to high-volume manufacturing.”
The expanded scope of collaboration will focus on next-generation 3D IC scaling and logic and memory integration for AI compute and memory architectures, with expected R&D programs to include:
New platforms for die-to-wafer hybrid bonding, building on the companies' existing Singapore Center of Excellence 
Scaling of thermo-compression bonding (TCB) and its surrounding process ecosystem
New die-on-wafer, die-on-die and die-on-panel integration platforms
Photonics-enabled interconnect applications supporting co-packaged optics and AI system scaling
Applied’s new, $5 billion * EPIC (Equipment and Process Innovation and Commercialization) Center in Silicon Valley represents the largest-ever U.S . investment in advanced semiconductor equipment and process technology R&D. The center, which will be operationally ready this year, is designed from the ground up to dramatically reduce the time it takes to commercialize breakthrough technologies from early-stage research to full-scale manufacturing.
*Capital spending is expected to scale over time to approximately $5 billion as customer projects commence. 
About Applied Materials 
Applied Materials, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMAT) is the leader in materials engineering solutions that are at the foundation of virtually every new semiconductor and advanced display in the world. The technology we create is essential to advancing AI and accelerating the commercialization of next-generation chips. At Applied, we push the boundaries of science and engineering to deliver material innovation that changes the world. Learn more at www.appliedmaterials.com .
Applied Materials Forward-Looking Statements
This press release contains forward-looking statements, including those regarding Applied's investment and growth strategies, the development of new materials and technologies, industry outlook and technology requirements, the plans and expectations for the EPIC Center, and other statements that are not historical facts. These statements and their underlying assumptions are subject to risks and uncertainties and are not guarantees of future performance. Factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied by such statements include, without limitation: the demand for semiconductors and customers' technology requirements; the ability to develop new and innovative technologies; the ability to obtain and protect intellectual property rights in key technologies; the ability to achieve the objectives of the EPIC Center; and other risks and uncertainties described in Applied's filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission, including Applied's most recent Forms 10-K, 10-Q and 8-K. All forward-looking statements are based on management's current estimates, projections and assumptions, and Applied assumes no obligation to update them.
About Besi 
Besi is a leading manufacturer of assembly equipment supplying a broad portfolio of advanced packaging solutions to the semiconductor and electronics industries. We offer customers high levels of accuracy, reliability and throughput at a lower cost of ownership with a principal focus on wafer level and substrate assembly solutions. Customers are primarily leading semiconductor manufacturers, foundries, assembly subcontractors and electronics and industrial companies. Besi’s ordinary shares are listed on Euronext Amsterdam (symbol: BESI). Its Level 1 ADRs are listed on the OTC markets (symbol: BESIY) and its headquarters are located in Duiven, the Netherlands. For more information, please visit our website at
www.besi.com .

The use of words such as “anticipate”, “estimate”, “expect”, “can”, “intend”, “believes”, “may”, “plan”, “predict”, “project”, “forecast”, “will”, “would”, and similar expressions are intended to identify forward-looking statements, although not all forward-looking statements contain these identifying words. The financial guidance set forth under the heading “Outlook” contains such forward-looking statements. While these forward-looking statements represent our judgments and expectations concerning the development of our business, a number of risks, uncertainties and other important factors could cause actual developments and results to differ materially from those contained in forward-looking statements, including any inability to maintain continued demand for our products; failure of anticipated orders to materialize or postponement or cancellation of orders, generally without charges; the volatility in the demand for semiconductors and our products and services; failure to develop new and enhanced products and introduce them at competitive price levels; failure to adequately manage costs and expenses in line with revenue; loss of significant customers, including through industry consolidation or the emergence of industry alliances; lengthening of the sales cycle; potential instability in foreign capital markets; the risk of failure to successfully manage our diverse operations; any inability to attract and retain skilled personnel, including as a result of restrictions on immigration, travel or the availability of visas for skilled technology workers; and the other risks detailed in the Risk Management section of our Annual Report. In addition, the United States and other countries have recently levied tariffs and taxes on certain goods and could significantly increase or impose new tariffs on a broad array of goods. Increased or new tariffs and additional taxes, including any retaliatory measures, trade restrictions and export regulations, could negatively impact end-user demand and customer investment in semiconductor assembly equipment, increase Besi’s supply chain complexity and manufacturing costs, decrease margins, reduce the competitiveness of our products or restrict our ability to sell products, provide services or purchase necessary equipment and supplies. title: How aluminium is made and why it matters The journey from red rock to the metal we use every day
content_excerpt: How aluminium is made and why it matters The journey from red rock to the metal we use every day. Aluminium is everywhere. It’s light, strong, and durable, making it the ideal material for things like window frames, vehicle parts, food or drink packaging and power cables .  But where does aluminium come from and how is it made? Understanding the journey from red rock to metal helps explain aluminium’s versatility and why the way it's produced matters.  Key takeaways:  Aluminium starts as bauxite, a reddish-brown rock found in the ground. Bauxite is refined into alumina, a fine white powder, which is then smelted into aluminium metal.  Aluminium is widely used because it’s light, strong, corrosion-resistant, conductive, malleable, and recyclable.  ...

title: October 23, 2026 Hydro's third quarter 2026: Solid results and strong performance
source: Norsk Hydro - News Subscription / Investor News Subscription
content_text:
Hydro's third quarter 2026: Solid results and strong performance
Hydro’s adjusted EBITDA for the third quarter of 2026 was NOK 9,089 million, up from NOK 5,996 million in the same quarter last year. Higher all-in metal prices and higher alumina prices contributed positively in the quarter, along with improved earnings in Recycling and Extrusions. The strong performance was partially offset by higher anode and energy costs in Aluminium Metal, increased energy costs in Bauxite & Alumina due to gas supply disruptions, a stronger NOK vs USD, and negative price area differences in Energy.
Alunorte resumed regular operations following temporary gas supply disruptions 
Free cash flow of NOK 1.4 billion impacted by higher metal prices and associated working capital requirements and prepayments
First metal produced at HalZero test facility, marking important milestone for carbon-free technology track
Commercial momentum continues for Hydro's low-carbon and recycled aluminium portfolio
New PPAs secured, further strengthening Hydro's long-term power position
Hydro delivered strong profitability in the quarter, with adjusted earnings per share increasing from NOK 1.0 in the third quarter of 2025, to NOK 2.3 in the third quarter of 2026. Free cash flow was NOK 1.4 billion, as strong adjusted EBITDA was partly offset by higher net operating capital, primarily driven by increased metal prices and associated working capital requirements and prepayments. While this development reflects the current market environment, improving cash conversion and working capital efficiency remains a clear priority going forward. Consequently, Hydro has updated its year-end capex guiding to around NOK 12.5 billion, down from NOK 13.5 billion, and net working capital guiding to around NOK 32 billion, up from NOK 30 billion. The twelve month adjusted RoaCE ended at 12.5 percent.
“Hydro’s third quarter results reflect strong operational performance amplified by market tailwinds. Record high liquid metal production from our Norwegian smelter system, combined with strong pricing throughout the quarter drove solid earnings and strong profitability. Operational excellence enables us to capture more of the upside when markets are strong and, more importantly, builds resilience when markets turn,” says Eivind Kallevik, President and CEO of Hydro. 
During the third quarter, disruption in natural gas supplies to Alunorte temporarily reduced production at the refinery. Through mitigating actions, including securing alternative LNG supply, Hydro maintained operational continuity and successfully restored alumina production.
Aluminium Metal benefited from higher all-in metal prices and strong operational performance, while Recycling and Extrusions delivered improved earnings supported by strong recycling margins. Hydro's Norwegian smelters increased liquid metal production to record levels, reinforcing Hydro's position as a reliable supplier of low-carbon aluminium to European customers. 
In parallel, Hydro experienced continued momentum for its low-carbon and recycled products, with leading brands like CHANEL Fragrances and Beauty , General Motors , and Mercedes-Benz integrating Hydro’s solutions in their product lines. 
“We continue to see strong demand for our low-carbon and recycled offerings from some of the world’s leading consumer brands. When brands like CHANEL Fragrances and Beauty and Mercedes-Benz choose Hydro, they place their trust in our quality, reliability, and ability to help them achieve their ambitions. That trust has commercial value and reinforces our confidence in the long-term opportunities for low-carbon and recycled aluminium,” says Kallevik.
Hydro reached an important milestone in the development of its HalZero technology by producing aluminium for the first time, demonstrating the core electrolysis technology beyond laboratory scale. The achievement marks an important step toward Hydro’s long-term ambition of eliminating emissions from electrolysis and anode production. Further testing, piloting and technology development remain before any potential industrial application. Enova awarded NOK 82 million in funding to support the concept development and planning of an industrial concept pilot.
“This is an important milestone and a significant step forward in the development of HalZero. Producing the first metal demonstrates that the electrolysis technology works and paves the way for the continued development of a game changing technology with the potential to enable emission-free aluminium production in the future,” says Kallevik.
During the quarter, Slovalco began the restart of primary aluminium production following the agreement announced in July on long-term framework conditions with the Slovak government. The restart commenced in late August, marking the return of capacity curtailed during the European energy crisis in 2022. The first phase targets an annual production capacity of 75,000 tonnes by the end of February 2027. The restart reflects the importance of competitive power, predictable regulatory frameworks, and effective industrial policy in maintaining and rebuilding Europe's industrial base.
Results and market development per business area 
Adjusted EBITDA for Bauxite & Alumina decreased compared to the third quarter of last year, to NOK 283 million from NOK 1,290 million, mainly driven by lower alumina sales prices, natural gas supply disruptions resulting in higher LNG sourcing costs and unfavourable BRL/USD exchange rate effects. This was partly offset by lower raw material costs and lower fixed costs. 
PAX traded up throughout the third quarter 2026 to USD 370 per mt at the end on the quarter, diverging from Chinese alumina prices moving down. Despite lower alumina production at certain refineries in Indonesia because of raw material supply challenges, the World ex-China alumina market was oversupplied in the quarter. China's alumina market became increasingly oversupplied during the quarter as new refinery capacity came on line. Chinese alumina prices were close to the marginal cash production cost. Approximately half of China’s alumina production depends on bauxite imported from Guinea. The government of Guinea is considering the possibility of restricting annual bauxite exports volume, but no formal announcement has been made. 
Adjusted EBITDA for Energy decreased in the third quarter compared to the same period last year, to NOK 411 million from NOK 828 million. The decrease is mainly due to a loss on price area differences compared to a gain in the same period last year.
Average Nordic power prices increased in the third quarter compared with both the previous quarter and the same quarter last year. The increase was mainly driven by weak hydrological conditions and higher power prices in Continental Europe. Price area differences between the south and north of the Nordic market were above the previous quarter and below the same period last year. The price difference between central Norway and northern Sweden widened significantly compared with both the previous quarter and the same quarter last year.
The Nordic hydrological balance at the end of the quarter was 13 TWh below normal, compared to 15 TWh below normal at the end of last quarter and 1 TWh below normal at the same time last year. Norwegian hydropower reservoirs were around 67.8 percent of full capacity at the end of the quarter, which is below the normal for this time of year of 82.8 percent. The distribution was uneven, with lower than normal levels in the southern and central Norway, and higher than normal levels in the north.
Adjusted EBITDA for Aluminium Metal increased in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the third quarter of 2025, to NOK 7,031 million from NOK 2,732 million, due to higher all-in metal prices, partly offset by lower sales volume, higher energy and carbon cost, and weaker USD to NOK. Global primary aluminium consumption was slightly higher compared to the third quarter of 2025, driven by a 3.0 percent increase in Asia. Primary consumption in the World ex. China is estimated to be down compared to the third quarter of 2025. The Middle East crisis continued to affect the aluminium market and prices during the third quarter. Following indications that the conflict might be nearing an end at the end of the second quarter, tensions increased again in the third quarter, directly contributing to higher aluminium prices. Throughout the quarter the market traded in a range between USD 3,100 per mt and USD 3,300 per mt. Consequently, the three month aluminium price increased slightly throughout the third quarter of 2026, starting the quarter at USD 3,076 per mt and ending at USD 3,170 per mt. 
Adjusted EBITDA for Metal Markets decreased in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the same period last year, to NOK 125 million from NOK 154 million, due to lower results from sourcing and trading activities, partly offset by higher results from recyclers. 
Adjusted EBITDA for Extrusions increased in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the same quarter last year, to NOK 1,189 million from NOK 1,107 million, driven by higher recycling margins in combination with increased sales volume, partly offset by higher maintenance cost, higher SG&A cost and negative currency effects mainly from stronger NOK/USD. 
CRU estimates that European extrusion demand increased by 1 percent in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the same quarter last year, following weaker market conditions in the first half of the year. Automotive demand remained positive, supported by continued growth in battery electric vehicle production. Non-automotive transportation also turned positive after a weak start to the year, while building and construction remained broadly stable in the quarter.
CRU estimates that North American extrusion demand remained broadly unchanged in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the same quarter last year, following a decline in the first half of the year. Commercial transportation continued to grow, supported by improving truckload rates, with further growth expected going forward. The industrial segment also remained solid, supported in part by continued datacenter investments. Automotive demand remained subdued, reflecting persistent headwinds in electric vehicle production.
Other key financials
Compared to the second quarter of 2026, Hydro’s adjusted EBITDA increased to NOK 9,089 million from NOK 8,923 million, mainly due to higher all-in metal and alumina prices and lower fixed costs in the third quarter of the year. This was partially offset by higher energy costs in Bauxite & Alumina due to gas supply disruptions and seasonally lower Extrusion volumes and margins.
Net income (loss) amounted to NOK 5,263 million in the third quarter of 2026. Net income (loss) included unrealized derivative losses, mainly on LME related contracts of NOK 204 million, environmental cost of NOK 111 million, rationalization charges and closure costs of NOK 81 million, and impairment charges on fixed assets of NOK 70 million. The tax effect on these adjustments reflected a standardized tax rate for taxable gains and tax deductible losses. Adjusted net income (loss) for the first quarter ended at NOK 4,372 million. 
Hydro’s net debt decreased from NOK 16.3 billion to NOK 15.4 billion during the third quarter of 2026. The net debt decrease was mainly due to positive EBITDA contributions, partially offset by net operating capital build, investments and negative other operating cash flow. 
Adjusted net debt decreased from NOK 22.8 billion to NOK 21.9 billion, mainly driven by the decrease in net debt.

content_text:
Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany Collaborates with NVIDIA, Microsoft and Dawn Health to Develop Novel Support Model for People Living with Rare Tumors 
Collaboration between with NVIDIA, Microsoft and Dawn Health to explore how AI-facilitated technology can help build an innovative model for PSPs. 
Subscribe
Share 
Icons revealed to the left 
21 Oct 2026 
| 
Darmstadt, Germany 
Collaboration to explore how AI-facilitated technology can help make patient support programs more individualized, responsive and continuously available to people living with rare tumors 
Collaboration brings together clinical and pharmaceutical expertise, digital health product development, and enterprise AI services 
Company aims to bring the model to patients with desmoid tumors and neurofibromatosis type 1 with plexiform neurofibromas (NF1-PN) 
Not intended for UK-based media 
Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, a leading science and technology company, today announced a collaboration with NVIDIA Corporation (Santa Clara, California, USA), Microsoft Corporation (Redmond, Washington, USA) and Dawn Health A/S (Copenhagen, Denmark) to build an innovative model for Patient Support Programs (PSPs). The four-way collaboration brings together pharmaceutical and clinical expertise, enterprise technology, AI services and digital health product design, with the shared goal of making specialist-level support more individualized, responsive and continuously available to patients, no matter how complex their treatment journey is.
“Across their treatment journeys, patients with rare tumors often describe challenges that extend well beyond clinical care, like navigating multiple specialists, complex regimens and repeatedly reconstructing their treatment story for each new stakeholder. Our integrated support ecosystem starts with the need. The goal is to truly transform how healthcare is experienced, not add another tool on top of it,” said Miguel Fernández Alcalde, Head of Global Commercial Strategy for Healthcare business sector of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany. “This solution is designed to make more continuous and personalized support available across small and geographically dispersed rare tumor populations, including patients who may have limited access to specialist care.”
Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany is collaborating on the design of a pioneering integrated support ecosystem tailored to individual needs of people living with rare tumors, their disease state and circumstances. In practice, the outcome is a AI-facilitated companion, available to patients 24/7. Every interaction is grounded in clinically reviewed content, with defined escalation pathways, and full traceability and audit capabilities. Designed to complement, not replace, the care patients receive from their healthcare team, the companion extends the reach and responsiveness of support, while a nurse or healthcare provider remains available when needed. The collaboration builds on and expands a previously announced partnership between the company and Dawn Health to support rare tumor patients.
The new model to be piloted in key markets in Europe, has an initial focus on rare tumors, specifically desmoid tumors and neurofibromatosis type 1 with plexiform neurofibromas (NF1-PN). These disease areas are known to have complex treatment pathways, and high unmet needs of patients, which makes the case for more consistent, higher-quality support particularly urgent.
The multi-way collaboration is grounded on a shared belief that bringing digital interactions, human services and structured data closer together could, over time, help build a more complete view of how a patient's needs evolve throughout their journey.
Three other relevant players in the technology space have key roles in developing this novel patient solution. NVIDIA contributes AI technology & services including NVIDIA Nemotron , NVIDIA Nemotron Reranking open model, NVIDIA NeMo Guardrails, NeMo Relay, NeMo Gym, NeMo Evaluator, NeMo Data Designer, to help power the program's performance and safety capabilities; Microsoft provides cloud services (Microsoft Foundry, Azure AI Search, the AI Red Teaming Agent as well as Azure Kubernetes Service, Azure SQL and Azure Monitor to run the Dawn Platform); and Dawn Health leads product development, regulatory experience, and the design of patient-facing applications based on the Dawn Platform offering.
Traditional PSPs have long been a cornerstone of the support pharmaceutical companies offer patients, providing structured, validated guidance throughout the treatment journey. As treatment and care pathways grow more complex, patient demand for support is rising, while the reach of these programs often cannot keep pace. Patients in small or dispersed populations, such as those with rare tumors, continue to have limited access to specialist care.

About Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany's Integrated Health and Medicines
Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany's Integrated Health and Medicines (IHM) brings together medicines, data, devices and human support to better understand patient needs, identify gaps in care, enable better-informed clinical decisions and deliver personalized interventions throughout the patient journey. A medicine marks the start of a patient's support, not the end of it.
Working across Rare Tumors, Specialty, Fertility & Endocrinology, and Cardio-Metabolic care, IHM builds integrated ecosystems, connected devices and decision support tools through its High Touch, High Tech approach: technology helps continuously understand patient needs, anticipate when and where support is required and enable personalized interventions, while healthcare professionals provide the human connection and clinical expertise where they add the greatest value.
Every solution is created with insights from patients, clinicians, and partners who will use it. In the U.S., for example, the company recently launched TGCT & Me, a free app built with insights from patients, healthcare professionals, and a patient advocacy group to help people navigate life with tenosynovial giant cell tumor (TGCT).
About Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany 
Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, a leading science and technology company, operates across life science, healthcare and electronics. More than 62,000 employees work to make a positive difference to millions of people’s lives every day by creating more joyful and sustainable ways to live. From providing products and services that accelerate drug development and manufacturing as well as discovering unique ways to treat the most challenging diseases to enabling the intelligence of devices – the company is everywhere. In 2025, Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, generated sales of € 21.1 billion in 65 countries.
The company holds the global rights to the name and trademark “Merck” internationally. The only exceptions are the United States and Canada, where the business sectors of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, operate as MilliporeSigma in life science, EMD Serono in healthcare and EMD Electronics in electronics. Since its founding in 1668, scientific exploration and responsible entrepreneurship have been key to the company’s technological and scientific advances. To this day, the founding family remains the majority owner of the publicly listed company.

content_text:
Hydro reaches key milestone in development of zero-emission aluminium technology
Hydro has produced aluminium using its new HalZero electrolysis technology for the first time. The milestone marks an important step in Hydro’s work to develop a new primary aluminium production process with the aim of achieving net-zero emissions.
Norway's Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre is handed the first metal made from HalZero electrolysis technology by Hanne Simensen, Executive Vice President Hydro Aluminium Metal. (Photo: Anders Vindegg / Hydro) 
Since 2016, Hydro’s technology teams have been working to develop HalZero , an entirely new process for producing primary aluminium, which could replace the technology used globally today, first patented in 1886. The new technology is based on converting alumina into aluminium chloride before electrolysis in a process designed to keep chlorine and carbon in closed loops. The long-term ambition is to eliminate CO2 emissions from both electrolysis and anode production, releasing oxygen instead of CO2.
Hydro has now produced metal from aluminium chloride for the first time at its research and test facility at Herøya in Porsgrunn, Norway. The test facility was built with support from Enova, a state enterprise owned by the Norwegian Ministry of Climate and Environment, which awarded NOK 141 million in 2023 for the construction and operation of the facility. The test center has been in operation since January 2026, and is being used to test the individual process steps in the HalZero technology.
“This is an important milestone for Hydro and Norway’s technology and research communities, and a significant step forward in the development of HalZero. Producing the first metal demonstrates the technology developed in partnership with leading Norwegian research institutions, including NTNU and SINTEF, works. It paves the way for the continued development, maturation and testing of a technology with the potential to enable emission-free aluminium production in the future,” says Eivind Kallevik, President and CEO of Hydro.
HalZero is a long-term technology development program and one of Hydro’s most demanding technology initiatives in decades. Producing the first metal represents a major step forward, although several years of targeted testing and piloting remain before the technology could be ready for industrial use.
The main HalZero processes are being tested at the Porsgrunn facility. At this stage, production still generates CO2 emissions. The next step will focus on developing an industrial concept pilot, with the ambition of integrating and testing all the necessary process steps together.
The purpose of the pilot will be to establish the basis for the further industrial scaling of HalZero, with the aim of achieving net-zero emissions from primary aluminium production.
“Aluminium is a critical material for the energy transition and for transport, buildings, and infrastructure. If the world is to succeed in reducing emissions, we must also transform the way aluminium is produced. Developing an entirely new technology is demanding and takes time, but Hydro has both the expertise and a responsibility to help move the aluminium industry forward. That is what we are working to achieve with HalZero,” says Kallevik.
At Hydro’s Technology Center at Herøya in Porsgrunn, Norway, technologists are developing the HalZero production technology. (Photo: Narrativ) 
Hydro has invested significant resources in developing HalZero over several years. Funds from the climate and energy component of Norway’s CO2 compensation scheme are also used to support this work. Further progress depends on using the test facility over the coming years for systematic learning, testing and continued technology development. The experience gained at the test center will provide the basis for further work on the industrial concept pilot and subsequent assessments of industrial scale deployment.
Enova has now granted an additional NOK 82 million for the development of the project’s next phase , an industrial concept pilot for HalZero.
About HalZero
Primary aluminium is currently produced mainly using the Hall-Héroult process. Developed in 1886, this electrolysis technology remains the dominant industrial method for producing primary aluminium. In the process, oxygen from alumina reacts with carbon anodes, generating CO2 emissions.
HalZero is Hydro’s proprietary technology for primary aluminium production. It is based on converting alumina into aluminium chloride before electrolysis. In the HalZero process, chlorine and carbon are kept in closed loops, enabling the process to eliminate CO2 emissions from electrolysis and anode production.
HalZero is part of Hydro’s technology roadmap towards net-zero emissions from aluminium production.

Enova supports development of zero-emission aluminium technology with NOK 82 million
Enova, a state enterprise owned by the Norwegian Ministry of Climate and Environment, has awarded Hydro close to NOK 82 million for a feasibility study for the next phase in the development of HalZero, Hydro’s technology for aluminium production with net-zero CO2 emissions.
The first metal from the electrolysis at HalZero. (Photo: Anders Vindegg / Hydro) 
The funding from Enova will be used for concept development and planning of an industrial pilot facility (Industrial Concept Pilot, ICP), laying the foundation for further development and scaling of the technology.
“The support from Enova enables us to further develop the plans for the next phase of HalZero. This is an important step in developing and scaling the technology toward potential deployment at industrial scale,” says Hanne Simensen, Executive Vice President of Hydro Aluminium Metal.
HalZero is Hydro’s long-term technology development program for a new primary aluminium production process in which carbon is reused in a closed loop, with the aim of eliminating direct CO2 emissions from production.
On October 19, 2026, Hydro marked a key milestone in the development of HalZero, producing aluminium with the new electrolysis technology for the first time .
At Hydro’s test facility at Herøya in Porsgrunn, key parts of the process are currently being tested and further developed. The facility, which was also built with support from Enova , enables Hydro to qualify the technology step by step at a smaller scale, build operational experience and reduce technical risk before further scaling to pilot facility. The experience and results from the test facility form the basis for the continued development of HalZero.
The planned pilot facility will be significantly larger than the current test facility and will bring together all the key process steps in one integrated facility. The aim is to demonstrate the technology under conditions closer to industrial operation, test how the different parts of the process work together and establish the basis for further scaling. The plan is to build the facility in Grenland.
“Developing technology for zero-emission aluminium production is both costly and demanding. It is therefore natural for Enova to support Hydro’s work on new solutions that can contribute to the transition to a low-emission society,” says Evy Glørstad, CEO of Enova.
The funding does not constitute a decision to build the pilot facility. Any future realization of the facility will depend on the results of further technology development, completion of project development and future investment decisions.
About HalZero
Primary aluminium is currently produced mainly using the Hall-Héroult process. Developed in 1886, this electrolysis technology remains the dominant industrial method for producing primary aluminium. In the process, oxygen from alumina reacts with carbon anodes, generating CO2 emissions.
HalZero is Hydro’s proprietary technology for primary aluminium production. It is based on converting alumina into aluminium chloride before electrolysis. In the HalZero process, chlorine and carbon are kept in closed loops, enabling the process to eliminate CO2 emissions from electrolysis and anode production.
HalZero is part of Hydro’s technology roadmap towards net-zero emissions from aluminium production.

title: ALUMINIUM 2026: Hydro invests to strengthen resilience across the aluminium value chain Hydro's exhibition stand at ALUMINIUM 2026. (Photo: Anders Vindegg / Hydro) Hydro will be present at the ALUMINIUM 2026 trade fair in Düsseldorf from October 6 to 8. During the fair, Hydro will present how it is future proofin ... October 6, 2026
content_text:
ALUMINIUM 2026: Hydro invests to strengthen resilience across the aluminium value chain 
Hydro will be present at the ALUMINIUM 2026 trade fair in Düsseldorf from October 6 to 8. During the fair, Hydro will present how it is future proofing customer products and businesses across European industry through investments in renewable power, recycling, partnerships, and production capacity.
Hydro's exhibition stand at ALUMINIUM 2026. (Photo: Anders Vindegg / Hydro) 
Since ALUMINIUM 2024, Hydro has entered several long-term renewable power agreements, invested in new production and recycling capacity in Europe, entered new partnerships with brands like Mercedes-Benz and CHANEL Fragrance and Beauty as well as customer agreements covering close to 360,000 tonnes of low-carbon aluminium for Europe’s electricity infrastructure.
The aluminium products from Hydro are critical to energy infrastructure, mobility, and building and construction as they contribute to future proofing customers. Value chain transparency, documentation, low-carbon and recycled content, and the way Hydro works with customers to deliver circular solutions demonstrates how aluminium is part of the solution.
The commitments come as aluminium is increasingly recognized as a critical raw material and Europe seeks to reduce vulnerabilities in strategic industrial value chains. Combined, the investments strengthen Hydro’s ability to supply responsibly produced aluminium through changing energy, market and geopolitical conditions.
“Disruptions in global supply chains over the past years underline how critical reliable access to aluminium is for Europe. As Europe’s largest primary aluminium producer, Hydro plays a key role in securing our customer’s access to renewable based, low-carbon aluminium from a transparent value chain. We continue to invest in production, in recycling and in renewable energy to provide our customers with this critical material,” says Eivind Kallevik, President and CEO of Hydro.
CEO Eivind Kallevik at Hydro's extrusion plant in Raeren, Belgium. The plant is specialized in extruding long lengths and precision-profiles, as well as anodized and machined components. (Photo: Christine Fon / Hydro) 
Securing renewable power for aluminium production
Competitive renewable power is fundamental to Hydro’s ability to produce and supply low-carbon aluminium to European customers. 
To reinforce this position, Hydro has entered into new long-term renewable power agreements for its Norwegian aluminium operations since ALUMINIUM 2024. The agreements provide increased predictability for stable, low-carbon aluminium production. 
Hydro is also investing NOK 1.2 billion in the Illvatn pumped-storage power plant , its largest hydropower development in more than 20 years. The project will increase flexibility in Hydro’s renewable power production portfolio and make better use of water resources.
Hydro will build a new pumped storage power plant in Sogn and as part of the project establish a new 8 kilometer tunnel from Fivlemyrane (1,018 meters above sea level) to Illvatn (1,382 meters above sea level). (Photo: Bosko Janjusevic/Hydro) 
At the same time, continued development of renewable power production and grid capacity is needed to maintain competitive industrial production, enable electrification and support new industrial activity. Hydro is therefore pursuing opportunities to develop additional renewable energy production alongside its long-term power sourcing.
“Long-term contracts, investments in existing hydropower plants and the development of new renewable generation are complementary measures. Together, they can provide greater predictability for industry while contributing to a stronger and more flexible power system,” says Kallevik.
Expanding supply for Europe’s electricity infrastructure
Europe’s electrification ambitions depend not only on expanding renewable power generation, but also on building and modernizing the infrastructure required to transport electricity.
Hydro is investing NOK 1.65 billion in a new wire rod casthouse at its Karmøy aluminium plant in Norway . The investment will add 110,000 tonnes of annual capacity for low-carbon aluminium wire rod used in power cables.
With a new wire rod casthouse at Karmøy, Hydro can produce more aluminium wire for a rapidly growing market. (Photo: Anders Vindegg / Hydro) 
Hydro has entered an agreement to supply up to 274,000 tonnes of aluminium wire rod to NKT through 2033 , and approximately 85,000 tonnes to Nexans between 2026 and 2030 . Together, the agreements cover close to 360,000 tonnes of aluminium for European power transmission and distribution infrastructure.
“By linking new industrial capacity with long-term customer commitments, Hydro is supporting more predictable access to a critical material for Europe’s electricity grid,” says Kallevik.
Keeping more aluminium in circulation, returning it to new products
Hydro reached a capacity of around 850,000 tonnes of annual post-consumer aluminium scrap recycling by the end of 2025, and is investing EUR 180 million in a new recycling plant in Torija, Spain . 
The facility in Torija will have an annual production capacity of 120,000 tonnes and will be able to process up to 70,000 tonnes of post-consumer aluminium scrap. Hydro has also i ntegrated Alumetal’s four plants in Poland and Hungary into its European recycling network , adding 280,000 tonnes of annual capacity for recycled foundry alloys.
Hydro is additionally working with customers and partners to return end-of-life aluminium to new products. The expanded partnership with Mercedes-Benz includes the introduction of Hydro CIRCAL recycled aluminium containing at least 75 percent post-consumer scrap into series production for the next generation of Mercedes-Benz’ large electric vehicles in Europe.
The fully electric Mercedes-Benz CLA in the electrolysis hall at Hydro Årdal, where Hydro produces low-carbon aluminium for European industry. (Photo: Halvor Molland / Hydro) 
In the Train2Train pilot led by Siemens Mobility , aluminium recovered from decommissioned trains will be recycled at Hydro’s facility in Ghlin, Belgium, and processed into new extrusion billets to produce rail components at Hydro’s extrusion facility in Harderwijk, the Netherlands.
In Norway, aluminium from the existing façade of an office building in Oslo is being recovered, recycled through Hydro’s European network, demonstrating how façade aluminium can remain in circulation through full material traceability. 
Hydro enables Norway’s first closed-loop aluminium façade in Oslo refurbishment. (Photo: Emilian Liliegren-Helgesen / Hydro) 
“These partnerships and projects demonstrate how recycling, traceability, and manufacturing can keep aluminium in circulation across European value chains. Collecting, recycling, and reusing more aluminium in Europe reduces emissions, preserves valuable resources, and gives customers access to products with documented origin and recycled content,” says Kallevik.
Restoring competitive aluminium production
In July 2026, Hydro’s joint venture Slovalco announced an agreement with the Slovak government enabling the restart of 75,000 tonnes of curtailed primary aluminium capacity .
Slovalco plans to invest EUR 100 million in the restart. Primary production at the plant was curtailed in 2022 amid high European energy prices. The restart comes as European production has declined and the region has become increasingly dependent on imported aluminium.
Slovalco will restart production of 75,000 tonnes of primary alumunium. (Photo: Halvor Molland / Hydro) 
“Europe has the industrial expertise and market demand needed to build competitive aluminium value chains. What we need is the long-term political commitment and predictable framework conditions that make investment possible. Hydro continues to invest because we see a future for European industry, with lower emissions, more recycling and a secure supply of reliable aluminium for our customers,” says Kallevik.
Hydro will present its investments and customer solutions at ALUMINIUM 2026 in Düsseldorf from October 6 to 8 under the theme “Future-proofing industries.”

title: October 5, 2026 Update on Alunorte gas supply situation
source: Norsk Hydro - News Subscription / Investor News Subscription
content_text:
Update on Alunorte gas supply situation
Hydro provides an update on the natural gas supply situation at the Alunorte alumina refinery.
Alunorte was informed in August 2026 by its supplier CELBA of disruptions to natural gas availability. Consequently, Alunorte has not received contracted gas deliveries and is currently sourcing gas in the market at spot based prices. Alunorte is in parallel progressing a long-term gas supply solution on competitive terms. 
The potential third quarter 2026 financial impact for Bauxite & Alumina from the reduced production and purchasing gas at prices above the contract price may be USD 75 to 100 million. The estimated gas arbitrage impact for Alunorte for the fourth quarter of 2026 is between USD 90-110 million.
Alunorte does not expect further interruption to gas supply as a result of the current situation and continues to manage the matter in close collaboration with infrastructure owner CELBA and the relevant authorities. 
The financial impact remains uncertain and is subject to gas prices, contractual developments, and the implementation of a long-term solution. 
Alunorte is also pursuing available legal remedies and other measures to protect its contractual rights and interests under the existing gas supply agreement.

title: Bayer appoints Dr. Christoph Koenen, MD, as Chief Medical Officer
content_text:
Bayer appoints Dr. Christoph Koenen, MD, as Chief Medical Officer
Not intended for U.S. and UK Media
Berlin, October 1, 2026 – Bayer today announced the appointment of Dr. Christoph Koenen, MD, as Chief Medical Officer, effective October 1, 2026. He will lead medical and scientific strategies across the organization and assume these responsibilities in addition to his current role as Head of Clinical Development and Operations of the Pharmaceuticals Division. 
“The Chief Medical Officer role reinforces Bayer’s commitment to keeping patient needs and patient safety at the center of medical and scientific decision-making throughout the product lifecycle,” said Stefan Oelrich, Member of the Board of Management of Bayer AG and President of the company’s Pharmaceuticals Division. “Christoph Koenen brings deep experience as a physician, former Chief Medical Officer, and global R&D leader. His leadership will help further integrate clinical development and medical activities as we advance our strategic focus in R&D on delivering transformative medicines to patients faster.” 
A physician and business leader with more than 25 years of global pharmaceutical experience, Christoph Koenen has held senior leadership roles at Bayer, Bristol Myers Squibb, Novo Nordisk, Boehringer Ingelheim, and GSK. Before joining Bayer in 2022, he served as Chief Medical Officer at Otsuka Pharmaceutical, where he oversaw global development, regulatory affairs, medical affairs, pharmacovigilance, quality, technical operations, value and access, and portfolio strategy. 
Christoph Koenen is committed to advancing innovation in clinical development, improving patient access to new therapies, and fostering collaboration across the healthcare ecosystem. He currently serves on the Board of Directors of TransCelerate BioPharma, supporting industry-wide innovation and the modernization of clinical research. Christoph Koenen holds an MD from Ruprecht Karls University School of Medicine (Heidelberg), an MBA from Schiller International University (Florida/Heidelberg), and is board-certified in Internal Medicine and Diabetology. 
Bayer focuses on therapeutic areas where the medical need is greatest, including oncology, cardiovascular and renal diseases, neurology and rare diseases, and immunology. The company is currently advancing around 30 projects in clinical development. 
About Bayer 
Bayer is a global enterprise with core competencies in the life science fields of health care and nutrition. In line with its mission, “Health for all, Hunger for none,” the company’s products and services are designed to support efforts to master major challenges presented by a growing and aging global population and create value through innovation and growth. The Bayer brand stands for trust, reliability and quality throughout the world. In fiscal 2025, the Group employed around 88,000 people and had sales of 45.6 billion euros. R&D expenses amounted to 5.8 billion euros. For more information, go to www.bayer.com . 
Find more information at https://pharma.bayer.com 
Follow us on Facebook: http://www.facebook.com/bayer 
Forward-Looking Statements 
This release may contain forward-looking statements based on current assumptions and forecasts made by Bayer management. Various known and unknown risks, uncertainties and other factors could lead to material differences between the actual future results, financial situation, development or performance of the company and the estimates given here. These factors include those discussed in Bayer’s public reports which are available on the Bayer website at www.bayer.com . The company assumes no liability whatsoever to update these forward-looking statements or to conform them to future events or developments. 
Bayer AG is a holding company with operating subsidiaries worldwide. References to “Bayer” or “the company” herein may refer to one or more subsidiaries as context requires.

Renishaw, a world leader in measuring and manufacturing systems, publishes this trading update for the
three months ended 30 September 2026, which contains unaudited information covering the first quarter
(Q1) of the FY2027 financial year.
Momentum continuing in early FY2027
Performance highlights
• Strong year-on-year growth in all three business segments and all three regions, building on acceleration
during FY2026.
• Continued momentum in demand from customers in the semiconductor and the aerospace and defence
sectors, with growth also coming through in wider automation and industrial markets.
• Disciplined investment in expansion of our manufacturing capacity.
FY2027 Q1 segmental revenue
Q1 revenue at actual exchange rates was 47% higher than a weak comparator in the prior year, resulting in
a record quarter that was 3% above FY2026 Q4. Q1 revenue at constant exchange rates* was 48% higher
than the previous year.
