STRATEGIC REPORT
Chief Executive Officer’s review continued
A simpler, more focused Renishaw
While the benefits of innovation are clear in this
year’s performance, our new structure has also
helped, with three segments that are more closely
linked to our customers and end-user markets.
As well as giving investors a better understanding
of our business, the changes support the continued
delivery of our strategy, with a single leader for
each segment accountable for every stage of
product delivery.
The new structure is having an impact on the
Executive Committee as well, with our new segment
directors, Louise Callanan (ST), Derek Marshall (IM)
and Steve Oakes (PM), bringing renewed focus to
our discussions. At the same time, our two newest
colleagues, Group Human Resources Director,
Clare Nicholls, and Chief Financial Officer,
John Shipsey, have brought fresh external
perspectives, complementing the deep expertise
of other Committee members to help plan the next
phase of our growth and innovation.
We continue to manage our business portfolio
to focus on core products. During the year we
completed the closure of the drug delivery aspect
of our neurological product line and we are
continuing to seek a new owner for the remaining
neurosurgical activities.
Responding to employee feedback
While restructuring the business has brought many
positives, I know this has not been the easiest year
for colleagues. The combination of our cost reduction
programme, followed by the rapid rise in demand for
some of our products, has created extra pressure
on our people and processes. So I am particularly
pleased that so many employees responded to our
latest engagement survey. A 78% participation rate
is good in any year, as was the 85% who responded
positively when asked if they feel proud to work
for Renishaw.
We’re addressing several key points raised in
the survey, including helping people feel better
connected to our strategy, developing clearer
career pathways, and making it easier for them to
do their job so that we can accelerate our growth.
6 Renishaw plc Annual Report 2026
Simplifying our processes to
accelerate growth
We are committed to simplifying and clarifying our
operating model – our blueprint for what we do and
how we work – while retaining what makes us special.
Our new One Renishaw initiative is focused on
developing common processes in our sales, logistics
and finance functions, supported by our new global
ERP solution, Microsoft Dynamics 365. While we
have faced challenges with deploying this system,
our dedicated team has worked incredibly hard and
has done a fantastic job supporting our customers
during the year.
Refreshing our ESG strategy
I’ve spent time this year working with colleagues
to refresh our environmental, social and governance
(ESG) strategy. The purpose of this review was to
refine our goals, remove outdated elements and
streamline our targets while retaining the ambition of
our original strategy. We explain these changes and
provide an update on our progress in our ESG review
on pages 37 to 48. We continued to make progress
against our strategy this year, most notably by
reducing the emissions intensity of the aluminium
and steel we bought in FY2026 by more than 20%
(versus FY2025), against a target of 15%.
Looking ahead
We made excellent progress in FY2026, with growth
in all three segments. We are well positioned in
attractive markets that offer substantial through-cycle
growth opportunities. Our innovation-led strategy to
deliver outperformance is also delivering results, with
significant progress in our emerging product lines.
FY2027 has started strongly as we continue to benefit
from the current upturn in demand for semiconductor
manufacturing equipment. We expect further strong
progress on revenue and profit in the year ahead.
Will Lee

What Australian Strategic Materials Gets Right About Rare Earth Manufacturing
Market Opinion 
Jack Lifton
October 31, 2026 
2 Comments
Last Tuesday, October 27, I visited Australian Strategic Materials’ Korean Metals Plant in Ochang, South Korea. I have been involved in the development, production, and marketing of less common metals for more than sixty years, and during that time I have visited a great many metallurgical plants, laboratories, and industrial research facilities around the world. I have also listened to innumerable presentations by promoters of proposed critical minerals projects. I can therefore say, from considerable experience, that the ASM Korean Metals Plant is one of the most impressive examples I have seen of what can be accomplished when metallurgical engineering, industrial management, and a clearly defined commercial objective are brought together.
The first thing that struck me was the operation’s scale and professionalism. The Korean Metals Plant occupies a complex of approximately 20,000 square meters, or nearly five acres, in the Ochang Foreign Investment Zone, about 115 kilometers south of Seoul. I was informed that the operation now employs 78 people. This is not a speculative project, a collection of laboratory apparatus assembled for visiting investors, or an artist’s conception of a future industrial facility. It is an operating metallurgical complex with installed production equipment, technical personnel, quality-control systems, and the infrastructure necessary to manufacture rare earth metals and alloys for demanding industrial customers.
The plant was opened in May 2022 and has since developed the capability to manufacture neodymium and praseodymium metals and neodymium-iron-boron strip-cast alloys. These are essential metallic feedstocks for manufacturing high-performance sintered rare earth permanent magnets. Producing a separated rare earth oxide is not the same as producing a metal, and producing a metal is not the same as producing a magnet alloy with the chemical composition and physical characteristics required by a commercial magnet manufacturer. Each step requires specialized equipment, metallurgical expertise, process control, and customer qualification. ASM has established an operating capability in the stages of this supply chain that remain particularly underdeveloped outside China.
The plant’s currently reported installed nameplate capacity is approximately 1,300 metric tons annually of neodymium-iron-boron alloy. ASM is carrying out a second expansion phase intended to increase this capacity to 3,600 metric tons annually. During the first half of 2026, the company completed the installation of eight additional molten salt reactors, bringing the total to twelve. A second strip caster, with a planned annual capacity of 2,000 metric tons, is also part of the expansion program. The existing installed capacity and the larger planned capacity must not be confused. The latter depends upon completion, commissioning, and successful operation of the additional equipment.
I was particularly impressed by the quality of the plant’s laboratory facilities. The quality-control and research and development operations appeared thoroughly modern, professionally organized, and appropriate to the requirements of an advanced metallurgical manufacturing business. This is a subject investors frequently pay insufficient attention to. In the rare earth industry, producing a metal or alloy is only the beginning of the manufacturing process. Reproducing the required chemical composition, controlling impurities, establishing consistent product characteristics, and demonstrating those characteristics to a customer is what distinguishes a commercially useful operation from an experimental one.
A modern quality-control laboratory is not an accessory to a rare earth metal plant. It is an essential part of the production process. Customers purchasing materials for high-performance permanent magnets cannot accept uncontrolled variations in composition or product characteristics. The value of a rare earth metal or alloy is therefore determined not simply by the presence of the desired elements but by the manufacturer’s ability to deliver a reproducible product that meets a customer’s specifications. The facilities I saw at Ochang gave me confidence that ASM’s management understands this distinction.
Equally impressive was the company’s commitment to research and development. Rare earth metallization is a specialized field in which incremental improvements in process efficiency, yield, impurity control, and equipment utilization can make the difference between an economically competitive producer and one that survives only through subsidies. The ability to investigate and implement such improvements within an operating manufacturing organization is, in my opinion, a significant competitive advantage.
ASM has also been developing the capability to produce the heavy rare earth metals dysprosium and terbium, which are particularly important in the manufacture of permanent magnets intended to operate at elevated temperatures. The company reported its first commercial sales of these metals in 2025 and has continued development of its heavy rare earth metallization equipment. This is an important undertaking because heavy rare earth metal production outside China remains extremely limited. Establishing a reliable, commercially scalable production process for these materials would substantially increase the strategic importance of the Korean Metals Plant.
I should emphasize that my favorable assessment of the facility is not intended to suggest that all of its installed capacity is already being utilized or that every product under development has reached sustained commercial production. ASM’s published operating reports make clear that production volumes are still being increased and that additional equipment is being commissioned. This is the normal progression of a developing industrial operation. What matters is that the company has established the physical, technical, and organizational foundation from which it can expand production in response to actual customer demand.
Perhaps the most encouraging aspect of my visit was the quality of the management professionals whom I met. I found them to be outstanding. They impressed me as technically knowledgeable, commercially realistic, and thoroughly familiar with the practical problems of operating and expanding a sophisticated metallurgical manufacturing facility. Their approach was that of industrial professionals focused on producing qualified materials efficiently and consistently, rather than promoters primarily concerned with how large their future production might become.
In my experience, competent industrial management is as important as the underlying technology. A metallurgical process does not become a successful business simply because it works in a laboratory. It must be engineered into a reliable production system, operated by trained personnel, supplied with appropriate raw materials, maintained economically, and integrated with customers’ purchasing requirements. The management team I met at Ochang appeared to understand these requirements exceptionally well.
This offers a larger lesson for governments and investors trying to establish rare earth industries outside China. Much of the public discussion still focuses on mineral resources, mining projects, and the separation of rare earth oxides. These activities are necessary, but they are not sufficient. The ultimate industrial objective is the manufacture of useful products, and the essential intermediate stages of metal production and alloy manufacturing cannot simply be assumed into existence.
The Korean Metals Plant demonstrates that these intermediate capabilities can be established outside China. It also demonstrates why their development requires much more than access to a mineral deposit. The equipment, laboratories, operating procedures, technical personnel, management, and relationships with industrial customers must all be developed together.
ASM’s Korean operation is particularly relevant to the proposed reconstruction of the American rare earth permanent magnet supply chain. The United States does not need merely to announce additional rare earth metal and alloy production capacity. It needs to establish the ability to manufacture commercially qualified products, at predictable costs, in quantities justified by actual demand. The experience accumulated at Ochang could help establish comparable operations in the United States.
The question of raw material supply remains, of course. The Korean Metals Plant currently depends upon externally sourced rare earth feedstocks. The development of reliable sources of separated rare earth oxides outside China will therefore remain an important factor in the plant’s long-term competitiveness and supply security. But this should not obscure the achievement the plant represents. ASM has already established a significant portion of the downstream manufacturing capability that so many other companies are still proposing to build.
I left the Korean Metals Plant with a very favorable impression of both the facility and the people operating it. The complex is substantial, the laboratories are impressive, the installed manufacturing equipment is real, and the management professionals are among the most capable I have encountered in this industry.
For investors, the lesson is straightforward. Industrial capability should be judged by what has been built, what has been demonstrated, what can be produced reproducibly, and what customers are prepared to purchase. Announced capacity is not production, and production is not necessarily a qualified commercial product.
Australian Strategic Materials has made a substantial investment in establishing genuine rare earth metallurgical manufacturing capability in South Korea. I believe its Korean Metals Plant deserves recognition as an important achievement in developing a rare earth supply chain outside China.
After sixty-four years in this business, I am not easily impressed by industrial promises. I am, however, impressed by competent people operating real manufacturing facilities. That is what I saw at Ochang.

Rio Tinto Opens Two Argentine Lithium Projects Worth US$1.4 Billion
Written by Giann Liguid 
| 
Edited by 
Georgia Williams
Oct. 29, 2026 11:46AM PST
The company plans to invest approximately US$4 billion in growth capital across its Argentine lithium operations and expects to spend around 70 percent of it with local suppliers.
Tigarto / Adobe Stock 
Rio Tinto (ASX:RIO,NYSE:RIO,LSE:RIO) opened two lithium operations in Argentina's Catamarca province on Thursday (October 29), which is touted to add 25,000 metric tons of annual lithium carbonate equivalent (LCE) capacity once fully ramped up. 
To date, Rio Tinto has invested roughly US$1.4 billion in the Fénix 1B expansion and the new Sal de Vida operation. Both reached first production ahead of plan in the second quarter and are now ramping up.
Fénix began operating in 1997 as Argentina's first commercial lithium operation. The 1B expansion adds 10,000 metric tons of annual LCE capacity there, which raises the operation's total target to about 40,000 metric tons. Sal de Vida sits roughly 20 kilometers northeast of Fénix and targets 15,000 metric tons a year.
CEO Simon Trott linked the two projects to Rio Tinto's global target of 200,000 metric tons of annual LCE production capacity by 2028.
"Our focus now is on safely ramping up production, delivering reliable, high-quality lithium to our customers, and creating lasting value for our shareholders and Argentina," Trott said.
In Salta, Rio Tinto is building the US$2.5 billion Rincon project, which targets approximately 60,000 metric tons of annual battery-grade lithium carbonate capacity. 
In March, the company secured a US$1.175 billion financing package for Rincon from four lenders. 
Construction at Rincon started in 2025. Rio Tinto expects first production in 2028, followed by a three-year ramp-up to full capacity running across an expected lifespan of 40 years.
Outside Argentina, Rio Tinto took majority control of Nemaska Lithium (TSX:NMX) in Québec in February this year with a 53.9 percent stake and assumed direct management of the company. The Québec government holds the remaining 46.1 percent through Investissement Québec.
Rio Tinto said it plans to invest more than US$300 million in its Québec lithium business this year.

Rio Tinto Opens Two Argentine Lithium Projects Backed by $1.4 Billion
Rio Tinto has launched two lithium ventures in Argentina, underpinned by a total commitment of $1.4 billion, as the mining group accelerates its push into battery metals. The Fénix 1B expansion and the Sal de Vida operation, both located in Catamarca province, commenced first production during the second quarter of 2026, ahead of schedule, and are currently increasing output.
Once running at full capacity, the pair will contribute 25,000 tonnes of yearly lithium carbonate equivalent capacity, according to the company. At an inauguration event attended by President Javier Milei and Catamarca Governor Raúl Jalil, Rio Tinto chief executive Simon Trott said the developments draw on almost thirty years of lithium output in the province and the skills of the firm's Argentine employees. He also referenced the company's worldwide ambition of reaching 200,000 tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent annual capacity by 2028.
Project Details
The $530-million Fénix 1B expansion contributes 10,000 tonnes of yearly capacity, raising the site's overall target to about 40,000 tonnes. Fénix started producing in 1997, becoming Argentina's first commercial lithium operation. Rio Tinto is evaluating a further expansion, with an investment decision anticipated in 2028 or 2029.
Sal de Vida, a new lithium carbonate facility situated roughly 20 km northeast of Fénix, is designed for 15,000 tonnes per year. Its initial phase required an investment of $374 million.
Both operations belong to an integrated production hub in the Salar del Hombre Muerto, whose combined resource base stands at approximately 19 million tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent. Running the sites jointly enables infrastructure sharing, efficiency gains and efforts to lower water use. Fénix employs direct lithium extraction, whereas Sal de Vida uses conventional evaporation ponds.
Counting Fénix, Sal de Vida and Olaroz, Rio Tinto's nominal lithium capacity in Argentina totals roughly 100,000 tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent per year. Its wider Argentine holdings include a 66.5% interest in Olaroz and complete ownership of the Rincón project, which extends across Catamarca, Jujuy and Salta provinces.
Market Context
Argentina is projected to generate around 172,700 tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent in 2026, a 48% rise over the prior year and over five times the 2018 figure. Between January and August 2026, lithium exports brought in $1.467 billion, up 190.5% compared with the same period twelve months earlier.
Rio Tinto intends to direct close to 70% of its planned $4 billion in Argentine lithium growth capital toward local suppliers. The spending dovetails with Milei's push to draw foreign investment via market-friendly reforms and the Large Investment Incentive Regime, which grants tax, legal and foreign-exchange advantages for 30 years to eligible projects exceeding $200 million in value.
Benchmark Mineral Intelligence projects worldwide lithium demand climbing from 2 million tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent in 2026 to 7 million tonnes by 2050, chiefly on electric vehicle and energy storage growth. Argentina's Mining Secretariat anticipates the country may surpass Chile in lithium output by 2029 and achieve yearly production of 573,000 tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent by 2035.

Wolfspeed and BorgWarner sign multiyear SiC agreement
Thursday 29th October 2026
Long-term supply agreement supports BorgWarner’s next-gen 800V SiC inverter platform 
Wolfspeed has announced a multiyear supply agreement for its SiC devices to support BorgWarner’s next-generation 800V SiC-based inverter platform as strategic partner. BorgWarner is using Wolfspeed’s Gen 5 1200V SiC technology in the inverter.

content_text:
SCHOTT Poonawalla Renamed SCHOTT Pharma India, Reaffirms Long-Term Commitment to Indian Pharma Market 
Written By : sheeba farhat Published On 2026-10-29T15:46:32+05:30   |   Updated On 29 Oct 2026 3:46 PM IST 
New Delhi: SCHOTT Poonawalla Private Limited will become SCHOTT Pharma India Private Limited, marking an important new chapter in the company's journey and strengthening its connection with the global SCHOTT Pharma organization.
The new identity more clearly reflects the India business’s place within SCHOTT Pharma’s global network and its role in advancing high-quality drug containment and delivery solutions for the pharmaceutical and biotech industries. It brings together the company’s strong manufacturing footprint, long-standing customer relationships and deep market expertise in India with SCHOTT Pharma’s global capabilities, innovation and scientific excellence.
For customers, partners and employees, this is a change in name, not a change in commitment. There is no change in ownership, management, employees, business strategy, operations, products, services or existing customer commitments.
The transition reinforces SCHOTT Pharma India’s long-term commitment to customers in India and international markets, while creating a stronger and more consistent connection to the global SCHOTT Pharma brand.
Building on a heritage of more than 140 years, the new identity brings the company’s heritage and future ambition under one global name, reflecting the values that continue to define SCHOTT Pharma: innovation, quality, scientific excellence and trust.
Also Read: TPG to acquire 35% stake in SCHOTT Poonawalla from SII 
SCHOTT Pharma India represents both continuity and progress: the same trusted business, capabilities and relationships, now with an identity that more clearly reflects who we are today and where we are headed.
Roy Joseph, CEO & Managing Director, SCHOTT Pharma India Private Limited, said, “SCHOTT Pharma India represents the next chapter of our journey, combining our strength in India with SCHOTT Pharma’s global innovation and expertise. We see significant opportunity to build on our capabilities, deepen collaboration with pharmaceutical and biotechnology partners, and advance drug containment and delivery solutions. As we move forward, our focus remains on growing with our customers and contributing to the safe and reliable delivery of critical therapies to patients worldwide.”
“SCHOTT Pharma India plays a critical role in patient care. With more than 3 billion containers produced annually, this company enables around 7,000 injections to reach patients every minute,” said Dr. Christian Mias, CEO of SCHOTT Pharma AG & Co. KGaA, SCHOTT Pharma India’s major shareholder. “The name change from SCHOTT Poonawalla to SCHOTT Pharma India reinforces our strategic partnership and confirms our long-term commitment to India as a key pharma hub.”
The new identity builds on the company’s strong foundation in India. During the COVID-19 pandemic, its pharmaceutical vials supported more than 4.3 billion vaccine doses worldwide, including 3 billion doses in India. As India’s only manufacturer of glass pre-fillable syringes and sterile formats, the company also strengthens local supply capabilities. Furthermore, the company continues to invest significantly towards manufacturing capacity expansions of pre-fillable syringes and cartridges, strengthening their ability to support the rapidly evolving needs of biologics, biosimilars, GLP-1 based treatments and other advanced injectable therapies.
Looking ahead, SCHOTT Pharma India will focus on expanding capabilities across pharmaceutical drug containment and drug delivery solutions, driving innovation through closer customer collaboration, and strengthening operational excellence and sustainability. These priorities will support the company as it responds to the evolving needs of pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies while contributing to India’s growing role in the global pharmaceutical value chain.
SCHOTT Pharma India is a manufacturer of advanced drug containment and delivery solutions, serving pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies across global markets. Based on innovation in specialty glass and advanced materials, the company offers a comprehensive portfolio of injectable drug containment and delivery products, including vials, cartridges, syringes and ampoules. Manufactured to stringent international quality standards, SCHOTT Pharma India’s solutions enable safe storage of vaccines and biologics. Through continued investment in innovation and operational excellence, and a strong focus on quality, reliability and customer partnership, the company addresses evolving healthcare needs and supports better patient outcomes worldwide.

[Shin-Etsu FY2026 Q2 Earnings Call] Japan's Shin-Etsu Chemical Posts Record Q2 Operating Profit of ¥212.1 Billion, Up 27% on AI Demand; Electronic Materials Running at Full Capacity, Full-Year Forecast Unchanged
Add preferred source 
Shin-Etsu Chemical reported consolidated results for the April-September 2026 period, with revenue of ¥1.4206 trillion (up 10.6% year-on-year) and operating profit of ¥385.9 billion (up 15.6%), marking substantial growth on both lines. Operating profit for the July-September quarter alone rose 27% year-on-year to ¥212.1 billion, a record for any quarter. Driven by expanding AI-related investment, the Electronic Materials segment generated revenue of ¥577.7 billion (up 16%) and operating profit of ¥218.9 billion (up 28%), accounting for more than half of segment profit, with production running at full capacity. President Yasuhiko Saito said top executives at customer companies are requesting additional supply, and that the company is working on capacity expansion and pricing terms. Meanwhile, softening PVC market conditions pushed Lifestyle Environment Materials operating profit down 16% to ¥86.2 billion. The full-year forecast targets record revenue of ¥2.7 trillion and operating profit of ¥700 billion, but was left unchanged after the assumed exchange rates were revised toward a stronger yen. Capital investment was raised to ¥380 billion to accelerate response to AI-related demand.

Japan's Shin-Etsu Chemical Posts Record Q2 Operating Profit of ¥212.1 Billion, Up 27% on AI Demand; Electronic Materials Running at Full Capacity, Full-Year Forecast Unchanged
Shin-Etsu Chemical's consolidated results for the second quarter of fiscal 2026 (April-September 2026), announced on October 27, 2026, showed substantial growth on both revenue and profit lines: revenue of ¥1.4206 trillion (up 10.6% year-on-year), operating profit of ¥385.9 billion (up 15.6%), ordinary profit of ¥415.1 billion (up 13.0%), and interim net profit attributable to owners of the parent of ¥286.9 billion (up 11.3%). Operating profit for the July-September quarter alone rose 27% year-on-year to ¥212.1 billion, a record for any quarter, with the profit margin improving 1 point from a year earlier to 27.2%.

Electronic Materials Generates More Than Half of Profit
The Electronic Materials segment drove results. Revenue came to ¥577.7 billion (up 16% year-on-year) and operating profit to ¥218.9 billion (up 28%), accounting for more than half of segment profit. Historic expansion of AI-related investment for data centers sent demand for semiconductor materials surging, and with supply tightening for some products, the company implemented precise supply responses and price revisions.
President Yasuhiko Saito said at the briefing that "expansion of the AI-related market is driving demand, other fields are also recovering broadly, and our electronic materials production is running at full capacity." He added that "the top executives of customers I have met and held meetings with recently are all requesting additional supply and making future supply volumes a priority." He made clear the company intends to pursue capacity expansion and price pass-through simultaneously: "Responding will require investment, so not only for wafers but for many of the items we handle, we are working on the necessary investment and on setting prices and other terms to support it."
On magnetic materials, he said the company is working with customers on urgent measures to minimize the use of heavy rare earths while diversifying procurement across multiple raw material suppliers.
By Segment: Functional Materials Profit Up 31%, Lifestyle Environment Materials Down 16%

The Functional Materials segment posted a large profit increase, with operating profit of ¥63.2 billion (up 31%), on sales growth of high-value-added products. "Our policy of dramatically growing functional and specialty products is unchanged, and we are concentrating on that. The results are showing up in a rise in the overall average unit price, which is leading to improved profitability," Saito said. Cellulose for pharmaceutical formulations also grew.
Meanwhile, the Lifestyle Environment Materials segment saw operating profit fall 16% to ¥86.2 billion on softening PVC market conditions. In the United States, domestic PVC sales volume in July-September rose 7% year-on-year according to industry statistics, but market prices fell 3 cents per pound in July. They held firm afterward, and Saito said the price increase announced in October is "expected to go through, even if not in full." "From our perspective, this month's sales pace in the U.S. is on par with September, and the outlook for November is not bad," he said, offering a cautious but positive view. In overseas markets, the company also pushed through a price increase in July, after which prices fluctuated, but "now we are able to raise prices," he said. Caustic soda market conditions are relatively stable.
Processing, Trading & Technical Services grew on solid demand for containers related to semiconductor wafers, with revenue of ¥75.1 billion (up 12%) and operating profit of ¥17.4 billion (up 28%).

Full-Year Forecast Unchanged; Exchange Rate Assumptions Revised Toward Stronger Yen
The full-year forecast targets record results: revenue of ¥2.7 trillion (up 4.9% from the prior year), operating profit of ¥700 billion (up 10.2%), ordinary profit of ¥770 billion (up 8.7%), and net profit of ¥525 billion (up 10.7%). The forecast was left unchanged from July.

Notably, the company left its earnings forecast unchanged even as it revised its assumed exchange rates for October onward toward a stronger yen — around ¥157 to the dollar (previously around ¥160) and around ¥176 to the euro (previously around ¥180). content_text:
Q3 2026 Results: Air Liquide accelerates, driven by sales growth and the launch of its strategic plan
Paris, France, 
October 29, 2026 
Press Releases
Group
Sales growth , driven notably by growth in Electronics and Industrial Merchant 
Record investments  since the beginning of 2026, strengthening a record backlog 
Execution of the first €1 billion share buyback tranche by the end of 2026 
2026 and 2027 outlook confirmed 
Commenting on sales in the 3 rd quarter of 2026, François Jackow, Chief Executive Officer of the Air Liquide Group , stated: 
“On October 5th, with the unveiling of BEYOND, our strategic plan through 2030, we opened a new chapter. Our ambition is clear: reach the next frontier in lasting value creation by accelerating operational performance, capturing all profitable growth opportunities, and evolving our capital allocation program to boost shareholder returns. 
BEYOND is already being implemented by our teams worldwide . Our third quarter is a perfect illustration, delivering robust performance driven by the momentum of our sales and investments in growth markets. As a reflection of our deep conviction in our strategic roadmap and our commitment to accelerating performance, we are announcing today the launch of the first €1 billion tranche of our share buyback program, to be completed by the end of December . 
Reaching nearly €7.3 billion as of September 30, 2026, our revenue is up +4.3% excluding currency and energy impacts and +3% on a comparable basis. Gas & Services activities (1) grew by +3.6% on a comparable basis, particularly in Industrial Merchant , which rose +5%, confirming a steady growth since the beginning of the year. Electronics  also acted as a key driver with a strong +12% increase, boosted by sustained semiconductors’ demand for AI, for which our carrier gases and advanced materials are essential. Geographically, Asia-Pacific  and the Americas stood out, advancing by +7% and +6% respectively on a comparable basis. The key development this quarter is the acceleration of volume growth in Electronics and Industrial Merchant segments, going beyond positive pricing effects. While subject to fluctuations in this volatile environment, this is a very positive sign. 
Concurrently, the Group continues to enhance its operational performance, achieving €441 million in efficiencies through the end of September. Our investments have reached new heights. Standing at €1.25 billion this quarter, investment decisions total more than €4.1 billion since the beginning of the year. Our investments in Electronics have almost doubled in just nine months compared to the full year 2025. This momentum propels our ongoing investments to an unprecedented level of €6.2 billion. » 
Air Liquide is therefore confident in its ability to increase its operating margin by +100 basis points (2) and to deliver recurring net profit growth, at constant exchange rates in 2026 (3) . 
The Group is also confident in its ability to improve its margin by +100 basis points (4) in 2027. This brings its total objective to +560 basis points over the 2022-2027 period.” 
Highlights 
“BEYOND” STRATEGIC PLAN 
Accelerating the Group’s lasting value creation with its new 2030 strategic plan. It embodies Air Liquide’s ambition to expand in the highest-potential markets and turn major global structural shifts into opportunities. 
This ambition targets three key objectives : 
A compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of +10% (±2%) over the period in recurring net Earnings per Share (5) , ensuring ambitious and profitable growth ; 
A recurring ROCE (6) above 11% in 2030, while maintaining a significant increase in industrial investments over the period, ensuring lasting value creation; 
And a confirmed environmental commitment , pursuing a 33% reduction in CO 2 emissions ( 7 ) by 2035 compared to 2020, ensuring a sustained societal commitment. 
In order to achieve the recurring EPS objective, three complementary levers will be flexibly deployed: 
A compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of +5% (±1%) (8) over the period in sales , outpacing industrial production by a factor of 2 to 3, 
A margin improvement of +400 to +600 basis points over the period (9) , 
A capital allocation of over €40 billion over the period (10) , made possible by the increased profitability initiated during the ADVANCE plan. More than half of this will be dedicated to higher industrial investments, bolt-on and strategic acquisitions. In addition, a significantly higher return for both institutional and individual shareholders will be ensured by combining a sustained, regular dividend growth policy with the launch for the first time of a 4 billion euros share buyback program by the end of 2028 (11) . 
Attention to all stakeholders - from customers to employees, shareholders to local communities - is reinforced with specific measures for each in the BEYOND plan, built on three pillars: Listen & Care , Growth , Performance . 
CORPORATE 
Successful issuance of a €2 billion multi-tranche bond on the Euro market, very significantly oversubscribed by investors. This new transaction reflects investor confidence in the implementation of the BEYOND strategic plan for 2030. The funds raised will support the Group's capital allocation and drive the development of the activities in future growth markets. 
Creation of a research chair “Artificial Intelligence for chemistry and through chemistry” by Air Liquide, the Ecole normale supérieure (ENS-PSL) and the ENS Foundation. 
ELECTRONICS 
Japan : To support market momentum in semiconductors and AI, more than €170 million invested to support a leading semiconductor manufacturer in the expansion of its manufacturing capabilities, notably an existing logic chip production facility. Air Liquide will build, own, and operate several production units to supply large volumes of ultra-pure gases. 
In the United States , the Group supports the expansion of its customers' sites.  In Idaho , more than USD 150 million invested to build, own and operate a new industrial gas production plant. The plant will produce large volumes of essential gases to manufacture advanced memory chips to meet the surging demand for AI in the U.S. and global markets. 
And supporting SK hynix in Indiana , USA : Investment of more than USD 170 million to build, own and operate two new industrial gas production units. They will supply ultra-pure gases  to SK hynix's first US site. 
INDUSTRY & ENERGY TRANSITION 
Texas, United States of America : More than USD 200 million invested in a new low-carbon gas production facility to support the development of the chemical industry in this US state. Air Liquide is strengthening its production capacity at its long-standing partner Oxea 's site in Bay City.  
Footnotes: 
[1] Representing over 97% of Air Liquide's revenue. 
[2] Excluding energy impact and the amortization of intangible assets recognized as part of Purchase Price Allocation following DIG Airgas acquisition. 
[3] Recurring net profit excluding exceptional and significant transactions that have no impact on the operating income recurring. 
[4] Excluding energy impact. See definitions in the appendix of the Capital Markets Day presentation available on the Air Liquide Group website. 
[5] Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) of recurring net Earnings Per Share from year-end 2025 to year-end 2030 at 2025 exchange rates, see assumptions and new definitions in the appendix of the Capital Markets Day presentation available on the Air Liquide Group website. 
[6] Recurring ROCE excluding strategic acquisitions defined as presented at the Capital Markets Day, see definitions in the appendix of the Capital Markets Day presentation available on the Air Liquide Group website. 
[7] Reduction in Scope 1 and 2 CO 2 emissions compared to the 2020 baseline year, based on scenarios compatible with a 1.5°C trajectory. 
[8] This lever is calculated as a CAGR end of 2025 to end of 2030 at 2025 FX and Energy price; it includes the scope effect of acquisitions. See definitions in the appendix of the Capital Markets Day presentation available on the Air Liquide Group website. 
[9] This lever is calculated as the sum of yearly operating margin improvements at the energy price of the previous year, over the period 2026-2030. See definitions in the appendix of the Capital Markets Day presentation available on the Air Liquide Group website. 
[10] Sum of investments, acquisitions, dividends and shares buyback programs over the period 2026-2030; Includes bolt-on and DIG acquisitions but no other strategic acquisitions. 
[11] The Board of Directors has approved a €4 billion share buyback program through the end of 2028.

Concurrently, the Group continues to enhance its operational performance, achieving €441 million in efficiencies through the end of September. Our investments have reached new heights. Standing at €1.25 billion this quarter, investment decisions total more than €4.1 billion since the beginning of the year. Our investments in Electronics have almost doubled in just nine months compared to the full year 2025. This momentum propels our ongoing investments to an unprecedented level of €6.2 billion. » 
Air Liquide is therefore confident in its ability to increase its operating margin by +100 basis points (2) and to deliver recurring net profit growth, at constant exchange rates in 2026 (3) . 
The Group is also confident in its ability to improve its margin by +100 basis points (4) in 2027. This brings its total objective to +560 basis points over the 2022-2027 period.” 
Highlights 
“BEYOND” STRATEGIC PLAN 
Accelerating the Group’s lasting value creation with its new 2030 strategic plan. It embodies Air Liquide’s ambition to expand in the highest-potential markets and turn major global structural shifts into opportunities. 
This ambition targets three key objectives : 
A compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of +10% (±2%) over the period in recurring net Earnings per Share (5) , ensuring ambitious and profitable growth ; 
A recurring ROCE (6) above 11% in 2030, while maintaining a significant increase in industrial investments over the period, ensuring lasting value creation; 
And a confirmed environmental commitment , pursuing a 33% reduction in CO 2 emissions ( 7 ) by 2035 compared to 2020, ensuring a sustained societal commitment. 
In order to achieve the recurring EPS objective, three complementary levers will be flexibly deployed: 
A compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of +5% (±1%) (8) over the period in sales , outpacing industrial production by a factor of 2 to 3, 
A margin improvement of +400 to +600 basis points over the period (9) , 
A capital allocation of over €40 billion over the period (10) , made possible by the increased profitability initiated during the ADVANCE plan. More than half of this will be dedicated to higher industrial investments, bolt-on and strategic acquisitions. In addition, a significantly higher return for both institutional and individual shareholders will be ensured by combining a sustained, regular dividend growth policy with the launch for the first time of a 4 billion euros share buyback program by the end of 2028 (11) . 
Attention to all stakeholders - from customers to employees, shareholders to local communities - is reinforced with specific measures for each in the BEYOND plan, built on three pillars: Listen & Care , Growth , Performance . 
CORPORATE 
Successful issuance of a €2 billion multi-tranche bond on the Euro market, very significantly oversubscribed by investors. This new transaction reflects investor confidence in the implementation of the BEYOND strategic plan for 2030. The funds raised will support the Group's capital allocation and drive the development of the activities in future growth markets. 
Creation of a research chair “Artificial Intelligence for chemistry and through chemistry” by Air Liquide, the Ecole normale supérieure (ENS-PSL) and the ENS Foundation. 
ELECTRONICS 
Japan : To support market momentum in semiconductors and AI, more than €170 million invested to support a leading semiconductor manufacturer in the expansion of its manufacturing capabilities, notably an existing logic chip production facility. Air Liquide will build, own, and operate several production units to supply large volumes of ultra-pure gases. 
In the United States , the Group supports the expansion of its customers' sites.  In Idaho , more than USD 150 million invested to build, own and operate a new industrial gas production plant. The plant will produce large volumes of essential gases to manufacture advanced memory chips to meet the surging demand for AI in the U.S. and global markets. 
And supporting SK hynix in Indiana , USA : Investment of more than USD 170 million to build, own and operate two new industrial gas production units. They will supply ultra-pure gases  to SK hynix's first US site. 
INDUSTRY & ENERGY TRANSITION 
Texas, United States of America : More than USD 200 million invested in a new low-carbon gas production facility to support the development of the chemical industry in this US state. Air Liquide is strengthening its production capacity at its long-standing partner Oxea 's site in Bay City.

HyProMag USA Completes Pre-Feasibility Study for Three-Plant Rare Earth Magnet Expansion
HyProMag USA LLC has completed a pre-feasibility study assessing a possible expansion of its proposed rare earth magnet manufacturing platform in the United States beyond its first plant in Northlake, Texas, according to Mining.com. The Northlake facility is in detailed engineering, with commissioning of its first phase expected in mid-2028. 
The company is developing rare earth magnet recycling and manufacturing operations aimed at building a secure domestic supply chain for neodymium iron boron magnets, which it describes as essential components for defense systems, robotics, electric vehicles, advanced electronics and AI infrastructure.
Three-Plant Expansion Concept
The study evaluates a phased strategy involving three new regional production plants supported by a centralized manufacturing, finishing and technology hub. The hub would produce commercial NdFeB magnet products in the U.S. from both end-of-life recycled feedstock and primary alloy material.
Combined with the Northlake facility, the platform targets total salable material production of roughly 6,000 metric tons per year by 2034, an increase of 4,474 metric tons per year above current production. The 2034 output would comprise approximately 4,192 metric tons of magnets, 1,305 metric tons of magnetic NdFeB alloy powder and 503 metric tons of other salable material.
Economics Exclude Northlake
The study's economics cover the three new plants and the Central Texas hub only, and do not include the Northlake facility, whose value is excluded from the results. For the three new plants, the study envisions post-tax net present value of $1.85 billion to $2.1 billion, a post-tax internal rate of return of 31% to 36% and a profitability index of approximately 2.8x to 3.3x. Those figures rest on forecast prices and a Class 3 capital cost estimate of approximately $656 million to $623 million, with payback of 3 years and 2.3 years respectively.
For the first plant under the study in 2030, all-in sustaining cost is estimated at approximately $41.6 per kg to $37.4 per kg of finished NdFeB products sold, including downstream processing and finishing such as plating and epoxy coating. Based on forecast market prices and product mix, the weighted average realized all-in selling price in 2030 is estimated at approximately $100.5 per kg.
The combined post-tax net present value of the proposed Northlake facility and the potential plants covered by the study is estimated at $2.6 billion to $2.8 billion. The updated post-tax net present value for Northlake is approximately $723 million, based on forecast prices and a capital cost estimate of approximately $167 million.
Executive Commentary
Chief executive Julian Treger said in a news release that the study confirms the opportunity to establish a significant domestic rare earth magnet manufacturing platform in the United States. He said the study demonstrates robust economics and a pathway to producing higher-value NdFeB magnet products for strategically important sectors including advanced manufacturing, energy, defense and AI-driven technologies. He also said the platform is designed with flexibility to use primary alloy feedstock alongside recycled materials, which the company sees as supporting supply chain resilience and long-term operational competitiveness.

[News] Applied Materials to Double BESI Stake to 20% on Hybrid Bonding Demand, Pending U.S. Antitrust Review
2026-10-27 
Semiconductors 
editor 
Applied Materials is strengthening its position in advanced chip packaging as demand for AI-related semiconductor technologies continues to grow. According to Reuters , the U.S. semiconductor equipment maker plans to increase its stake in Dutch company BE Semiconductor Industries (BESI) from 9% to approximately 20%, deepening a partnership focused on advanced packaging technologies for AI chips.
Applied Materials, BESI’s largest shareholder since acquiring a 9% stake in April 2025, has entered into an accelerated share purchase agreement to acquire additional shares in the company, subject to U.S. antitrust review. The company said it does not intend to increase its stake beyond approximately 20% or seek representation on BESI’s board.
The expanded partnership will focus on next-generation chip interconnect and packaging technologies for AI semiconductors. Applied Materials and BESI have collaborated on hybrid bonding technology since 2020, Reuters notes. According to ijiwei , BESI holds approximately 70% of the global hybrid bonding equipment market.
BESI’s Hybrid Bonding Technology Gains Momentum
Hybrid bonding directly joins copper interconnects and dielectric layers without conventional bumps, enabling denser connections between chips. According to Chosun Biz , the companies have jointly developed Kinex, an integrated die-to-wafer hybrid bonding system that combines Applied Materials’ expertise in etching, planarization, deposition and inspection with BESI’s precision die placement and assembly technologies.
BESI is a leading supplier of hybrid bonding equipment. As noted by ijiwei, its flagship Datacon 8800 CHAMEO ultra plus AC system offers alignment accuracy of 100 nanometers and throughput of up to 2,000 cycles per hour (CPH), highlighting the technology’s potential for high-volume manufacturing.
Demand for the technology is gaining momentum. Reuters reported on October 22 that BESI’s third-quarter orders rose 96% year over year to €342.6 million, while hybrid bonding equipment orders in the first nine months of 2026 more than doubled compared with the full-year 2025 level. BESI ‘s latest earnings release further shows that its hybrid bonding customer base has expanded to 23, with cumulative equipment demand exceeding 215 systems.
Meanwhile, Chinese equipment makers are also advancing their hybrid bonding capabilities. According to ijiwei, Piotech generated RMB 136 million in hybrid bonding equipment revenue in 2025, up 41.92% year over year, and secured repeat orders for its wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding systems.

Infineon to establish Europe's first volume 300mm GaN facility
Tuesday 27th October 2026
€1.1 billion investment in the Villach site Austria to become global competence centre for power semiconductors 
Infineon is establishing the world’s first high-volume manufacturing facility for next-generation GaN power semiconductors on 300mm wafers in Europe. As part of the project, Infineon will invest around €1.1 billion in its existing cleanroom facilities at the Villach site in Austria by 2034.
Production is scheduled to start by the end of 2027. Infineon’s investment addresses the rapidly growing demand for high-performance power supply solutions. GaN enables significant efficiency gains in numerous applications, such as AI data centres, energy infrastructure, e-mobility, robotics and consumer electronics.  
'By establishing high-volume manufacturing on 300mm wafers, we will be the first company in the world to bring GaN power electronics into volume production,” says Jochen Hanebeck, CEO of Infineon Technologies AG. “In doing so, we are paving the way for the widespread use of GaN in a wide range of key applications in areas such as artificial intelligence, energy infrastructure, e- mobility and robotics. This new, state-of-the-art manufacturing facility translates innovation leadership into direct customer benefits.” 
Christian Stocker, Federal Chancellor of the Republic of Austria: “With Infineon’s billion-euro investment, we are witnessing one of the largest single investments in the history of Austria’s high- tech industry. This is not only a strong commitment to Austria as a business location but also helps ensure that the future of the semiconductor industry will not be shaped solely in Asia or the United States, but also in Austria and Europe."
The investment is being supported under the European Chips Act. The European Commission approved €319 million in state aid. The formal funding commitment by the Austrian Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs, Energy and Tourism is expected within the stipulated time limits.

HyProMag Outlines Three-Plant Expansion to Quadruple US Rare Earth Magnet Output
HyProMag , a scrap recycler, has outlined a scenario involving three plants that would quadruple its rare earth magnet production, Mining Weekly reports. The HyProMag USA subsidiary of TSX-V- and Aim-listed Mkango Magnetic Materials has finished an independent prefeasibility study on potentially expanding its planned US rare earth magnet manufacturing platform beyond its initial Northlake, Texas, plant. 
The Northlake facility is in detailed engineering, with Phase 1 commissioning targeted for mid-2028. The study assesses a phased build-out to three regional production plants backed by a centralised manufacturing, finishing and technology hub called the Central Texas Hub, making commercial neodymium-iron-boron magnet products in the US from end-of-life recycled feedstock and primary alloy material.
Alongside the Northlake Texas facility, the platform aims for total saleable material of roughly 6 000 t/y by 2034, which is 4 474 t/y more than the standalone Northlake scenario. Mkango expects HyProMag's total magnetic material production by 2034 to reach 4 192 t/y of magnets, 1 305 t/y of magnetic NdFeB alloy powder and 503 t/y of other saleable material.
The study draws on engineering and development work already completed for the Northlake facility and sets out how HyProMag could evolve from a Hydrogen Processing of Magnet Scrap-enabled magnet recycler into a fully integrated producer of commercial rare earth magnet products for US customers. HyProMag considers the platform to combine the cost advantages and operational flexibility of recycled and primary alloy feedstocks, offering a flexible and scalable route to magnet manufacturing. The company could also benefit from potential future access to primary sourced feedstock from Mkango under certain supply rights.
The study examined three new production plants in South Carolina, Nevada and a second Texas location, which would run alongside the Northlake facility. Each plant is meant to process feedstock, operate the HPMS process and produce unfinished sintered NdFeB blocks, which could then be moved to the Central Texas Hub for advanced manufacturing and finishing.
A key finding was optimisation of the manufacturing configuration to raise output of higher-value NdFeB magnet products. The study outlines a potential four-fold rise in US magnet production capacity, from 1 048 t/y of NdFeB magnets at Northlake Texas alone to about 4 192 t/y across four plants by 2034. The plants are designed to recover and reprocess manufacturing residues, including magnet machining end cuts through the HPMS process, maximising use of rare earth materials.
The study assessed two development options based on modular production systems. In the first, the plants use recycled feedstock only, applying HPMS recycling of magnet scrap to produce NdFeB alloy powder, sintered magnet blocks and finished magnets. The second envisions recycled and primary feedstocks, with additional capital expenditure to support primary NdFeB alloy as a feedstock.
Case 1 delivered the strongest project economics with an after-tax net present value of $2.06-billion, an internal rate of return of 36% and a payback period of 2.3 years, for a capital cost of $623-million. Case 2 showed a net present value of $1.8-billion, an internal rate of return of 31% and a payback period of three years, for a capital cost of $656-million. The combined after-tax net present value range of the proposed Northlake facility and the potential study plants is estimated between $2.6-billion and $2.8-billion.
Mkango said the study demonstrates robust economics and a pathway to producing higher-value NdFeB magnet products for strategically important sectors. HyProMag founder Allan Walton said the platform's objective has always been to demonstrate that HPMS technology can recover rare earth magnetic materials and convert them into high-performance commercial magnet products, and that the study outlines a pathway to scaling that capability through an integrated manufacturing platform incorporating magnet production, finishing and product qualification. He added that the enhanced production configuration would support manufacture of a broader range of commercial magnet products for demanding industrial applications, while finishing, quality assurance and product development capabilities provide a foundation for continued product optimisation and customer qualification.

query: ("Infineon" OR "Infineon Technologies") ("press release" OR "investor relations" OR earnings OR announcement OR investment OR expansion OR acquisition OR partnership OR Korea) after:2026-10-01 before:2026-11-01
content_text:
Sign Up to Our Free Weekly E-Brief
Media Kit Download & Details 
News: Microelectronics 
27 October 2026 
Infineon establishing first high-volume fab for GaN power semiconductors on 300mm wafers in Europe
Infineon Technologies AG of Munich, Germany is establishing the world’s first high-volume manufacturing facility for gallium nitride (GaN) power semiconductors on 300mm wafers in Europe. As part of the project, the firm will invest about €1.1bn in its existing cleanroom facilities at the site in Villach, Austria by 2034. Leveraging both the existing and upgraded infrastructure will enable efficient and cost-effective expansion of manufacturing capacity, it is reckoned. Production is scheduled to start by the end of 2027. 
Infineon’s investment addresses the rapidly growing demand for high-performance power supply solutions, as gallium nitride enables significant efficiency gains in applications such as AI data centers, energy infrastructure, e-mobility, robotics and consumer electronics. 
Picture: Infineon’s site in Villach, Austria. 
Two years ago, Infineon achieved the milestone of processing the world’s first 300mm GaN wafers. Compared with 200mm wafers, the 300mm diameter enables the production of 2.3 times as many chips per wafer. Infineon is now transferring this more efficient technology to the first high-volume manufacturing facility serving customers. 
“This substantial investment shows our clear commitment to strengthening the European semiconductor ecosystem and Europe’s technological sovereignty. By establishing high-volume manufacturing on 300mm wafers, we will be the first company in the world to bring gallium nitride power electronics into volume production,” says Infineon’s CEO Jochen Hanebeck. “In doing so, we are paving the way for the widespread use of gallium nitride in a wide range of key applications in areas such as artificial intelligence, energy infrastructure, e-mobility and robotics,” he adds. 
“We are witnessing one of the largest single investments in the history of Austria’s high-tech industry,” states Christian Stocker, Federal Chancellor of the Republic of Austria. “This is not only a strong commitment to Austria as a business location but also helps ensure that the future of the semiconductor industry will not be shaped solely in Asia or the USA, but also in Austria and Europe,” he adds. 
“Europe currently accounts for only around 10% of global chip production… We must also manufacture this key technology in Europe,” says Wolfgang Hattmannsdorfer, Austrian Federal Minister for Economic Affairs. “Austria is already a leader in energy-efficient chips. Relative to our population, we rank first in the EU in business R&D spending in the semiconductor sector. With our industrial strategy, we intend to build on this lead and not only research new technologies but also manufacture them on an industrial scale,” he adds. “Every job in the chip industry can provide six additional jobs across the broader economy. That is why we intend to support Infineon’s new chip production with up to €319m — subject to clear funding criteria for the location. This will ensure that public funds strengthen value creation and jobs in Austria over the long term.” 
The investment is being supported under the European Chips Act. The European Commission has approved the €319m in state aid. The formal funding commitment by the Austrian Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs, Energy and Tourism is expected within the stipulated time limits.
“Competitiveness and technological sovereignty emerge where excellent research is translated into industrial value creation. This is precisely where our flagship project comes in. From Austria, we are bringing innovation into industrial application, strengthening our technological leadership and securing highly skilled jobs,” says Infineon Technologies Austria AG’s CEO Sabine Herlitschka. “The entire Austrian semiconductor ecosystem benefits — from research organizations and universities to industrial partners. We are thus sustainably strengthening Europe’s competitiveness and strategic autonomy in microelectronics.”
Infineon reckons that the investment strengthens Villach’s role as a global competence center for power electronics and new semiconductor materials. Infineon Austria currently employs about 5800 people, including 4800 at the Villach site (as of end-September 2025). Together with universities, research institutions, start-ups and industry partners, Infineon forms the core of a microelectronics ecosystem in southern Austria. The establishment of the new 300mm GaN manufacturing facility is also expected to create synergies with the power electronics R&D activities in Villach.

content_text:
Applied Materials Raises BE Semiconductor Stake to 20%, Deepening AI Advanced Packaging Push; Deal Awaits U.S. Antitrust Review
Add preferred source 2 
Applied Materials announced it will raise its stake in Dutch packaging equipment maker BE Semiconductor Industries from 9% to approximately 20%, having signed an accelerated share purchase agreement, with the deal still pending U.S. antitrust review. Applied Materials became BE Semiconductor's largest shareholder after first taking a stake in April 2025, and the increased holding is aimed at AI chip advanced packaging. The two companies have collaborated on hybrid bonding technology since 2020 and have jointly developed the Kinex integrated die-to-wafer system. Applied Materials said it does not intend to push its stake above 20% or seek board seats. BE Semiconductor holds roughly 70% of the global hybrid bonding equipment market, with third-quarter orders up 96% year over year, and hybrid bonding equipment orders in the first nine months of 2026 already more than double the full-year 2025 level.
Key Elements 
Applied Materials BE Semiconductor Industries hybrid bonding EPIC Center Prabh Raja ASML Kinex Piotech 
U.S. semiconductor equipment giant Applied Materials announced Monday that it will raise its stake in Dutch packaging equipment maker BE Semiconductor Industries (BESI) from the current 9% to approximately 20%, deepening cooperation between the two companies in advanced packaging for artificial intelligence (AI) chips. The increased holding has been signed under an accelerated share purchase agreement but still requires U.S. antitrust review.
Applied Materials became the largest shareholder of the Dutch company after first taking a 9% stake in April 2025. At that time, BE Semiconductor had a market value of about $13 billion. Under the plan, the stake will approach 20% once the increase is completed. However, Applied Materials made clear that at this stage it does not intend to push its holding above 20% or seek seats on BE Semiconductor's board, indicating that this is a long-term strategic investment centered on technology cooperation rather than a move toward a full acquisition.
The expanded cooperation focuses on next-generation chip interconnection and packaging technology, with the goal of supporting the next generation of AI semiconductors. The two companies have jointly invested in hybrid bonding process development since 2020, a technology regarded as a key link in advanced packaging and mainly used for high-performance chips.
Hybrid bonding is characterized by directly bonding copper interconnects and dielectric layers without the need for traditional bumps, allowing a substantial increase in connection density between chips. The two companies have jointly developed the Kinex integrated die-to-wafer hybrid bonding system, combining Applied Materials' expertise in etching, planarization, deposition and inspection with BE Semiconductor's technology in high-precision die placement and assembly. BE Semiconductor also recently formally joined Applied Materials' newly established chip equipment research organization, the EPIC Center.
Prabh Raja, president of Applied Materials' Semiconductor Products Group, said in a statement: "We look forward to further deepening our strategic collaboration with Besi to deliver the innovative products and technologies customers need to scale AI systems."
From a market structure perspective, BE Semiconductor holds a critical position in the advanced packaging equipment sector. According to market data, BE Semiconductor accounts for about 70% of the global hybrid bonding equipment market. Its flagship model, the Datacon 8800 CHAMEO ultra plus AC, achieves alignment accuracy of up to 100 nanometers and a throughput of up to 2,000 cycles per hour, with volume production potential.
Demand-side momentum is also strengthening. BE Semiconductor's third-quarter orders surged 96% year over year to €342.6 million (approximately $382.0 million); hybrid bonding equipment orders in the first nine months of 2026 were already more than double the full-year 2025 level. The company's latest financial report shows that its hybrid bonding customer base has expanded to 23 companies, with cumulative equipment demand exceeding 215 units.
It is worth noting that last week the market briefly worried that Dutch semiconductor equipment leader ASML might become a competitor to BE Semiconductor in the hybrid bonding arena, which BE Semiconductor has denied. Against the backdrop of advanced packaging becoming key to the AI chip computing power race, alliances and competitive-cooperative relationships among equipment makers are rapidly intensifying.
On the other hand, Chinese equipment makers are also catching up in hybrid bonding technology. China's Piotech recorded hybrid bonding equipment revenue of CNY 136 million (approximately $20.4 million) in 2025, up 41.92% year over year, and has secured repeat orders for wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding systems, meaning that this niche market previously dominated by a small number of vendors is gradually seeing new suppliers emerge.
For investors, the most direct significance of this deal is that Applied Materials is betting its resources on the "back-end" packaging link of AI chips. As advancing Moore's Law becomes increasingly difficult, improvements in chip performance increasingly depend on advanced packaging and heterogeneous integration, and hybrid bonding is one of the highest-barrier technologies in this area. By tying up with BE Semiconductor through a stake purchase rather than an acquisition, Applied Materials can share technology and customers while avoiding the operational risks and regulatory resistance of full integration.
However, the deal still must pass U.S. antitrust review, and the timetable and conditions remain uncertain. Applied Materials has also stated that it will not pursue board seats or increase its stake further, and whether the cooperation can be translated into substantive orders and revenue contribution will be a key focus for the market going forward.
